```sql
  Objective: For each day of the week in 2021, count total Stack Overflow questions
  and among them, count those that received at least one answer within 1 hour of creation.
  Compute the percentage of such questions per day.
*/
WITH questions_2021 AS (
  SELECT
    id,
    creation_date,
    -- Extract the full day name (e.g., 'Monday')
    FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%A', creation_date) AS day_of_week
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM creation_date) = 2021
),
question_answered_flag AS (
  SELECT
    q.id,
    q.day_of_week,
    -- Check if there exists at least one answer within 1 hour of question creation
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` a
      WHERE a.parent_id = q.id
        AND a.creation_date >= q.creation_date
        AND a.creation_date < TIMESTAMP_ADD(q.creation_date, INTERVAL 1 HOUR)
    ) AS answered_within_1h
  FROM questions_2021 q
)
SELECT
  day_of_week,
  COUNT(*) AS total_questions,
  COUNTIF(answered_within_1h) AS answered_within_1h,
  ROUND(COUNTIF(answered_within_1h) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 4) AS percentage_answered_within_1h
FROM question_answered_flag
GROUP BY day_of_week
ORDER BY
  -- Order by calendar day-of-week (Monday = 1, Sunday = 7)
  CASE day_of_week
    WHEN 'Monday'    THEN 1
    WHEN 'Tuesday'   THEN 2
    WHEN 'Wednesday' THEN 3
    WHEN 'Thursday'  THEN 4
    WHEN 'Friday'    THEN 5
    WHEN 'Saturday'  THEN 6
    WHEN 'Sunday'    THEN 7
  END;
```
</details>

### 115. bq124 (DB: `fhir_synthea`)
**Question**: Among all patients, how many individuals remain alive (i.e., with no recorded deceased.dateTime), have a diagnosis of either Diabetes or Hypertension, and are prescribed at least seven distinct active medications?

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify alive patients (no deceased.dateTime recorded)
WITH alive_patients AS (
  SELECT id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.patient`
  WHERE deceased.dateTime IS NULL
),

-- Step 2: Among alive patients, find those diagnosed with Diabetes or Hypertension
-- Use condition table, check code text or display for keywords
patients_with_diabetes_or_hypertension AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT p.id
  FROM alive_patients p
  INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.condition` c
    ON p.id = c.subject.patientId
  CROSS JOIN UNNEST(c.code.coding) AS coding
  WHERE LOWER(coding.display) LIKE '%diabetes%'
     OR LOWER(coding.display) LIKE '%hypertension%'
),

-- Step 3: Among those, find patients prescribed at least 7 distinct active medications
-- active medication: medication_request.status = 'active'
-- distinct medication: use medication.medication.codeableConcept.coding.code (or medication.reference.medicationId)
patients_with_min_7_active_meds AS (
  SELECT p.id
  FROM patients_with_diabetes_or_hypertension p
  INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.medication_request` mr
    ON p.id = mr.subject.patientId
  CROSS JOIN UNNEST(mr.medication.codeableConcept.coding) AS med_coding
  WHERE mr.status = 'active'
  GROUP BY p.id
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT med_coding.code) >= 7
)

-- Final count
SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count
FROM patients_with_min_7_active_meds;
```
</details>

|         53741008 | Coronary Heart Disease                  |                4 |
|        162864005 | Body mass index 30+ - obesity (finding) |                3 |

*... and 3 more rows.*

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
N/A
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Step 1: Patients alive with last name starting with 'A'
  patient_a AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT p.id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.patient` p,
         UNNEST(p.name) AS n
    WHERE n.family IS NOT NULL
      AND LOWER(n.family) LIKE 'a%'
      AND NOT COALESCE(p.deceased.boolean, FALSE)   -- alive: deceased is NULL or boolean is FALSE
  ),

  -- Step 2: Patients with exactly one distinct condition (code)
  patients_single_cond AS (
    SELECT c.subject.patientId
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.condition` c
    WHERE c.subject.patientId IN (SELECT id FROM patient_a)
      AND c.code.coding[SAFE_OFFSET(0)].code IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY c.subject.patientId
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.code.coding[SAFE_OFFSET(0)].code) = 1
  ),

  -- Step 3: Get the single condition code and display for each patient
  patient_cond AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM (
      SELECT c.subject.patientId,
             c.code.coding[SAFE_OFFSET(0)].code AS condition_code,
             c.code.coding[SAFE_OFFSET(0)].display AS condition_display,
             ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.subject.patientId ORDER BY c.id) AS rn
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.condition` c
      WHERE c.subject.patientId IN (SELECT patientId FROM patients_single_cond)
        AND c.code.coding[SAFE_OFFSET(0)].code IS NOT NULL
    )
    WHERE rn = 1
  ),

  -- Step 4: Count distinct active medications per patient
  patient_drugs AS (
    SELECT mr.subject.patientId,
           mr.medication.codeableConcept.coding[SAFE_OFFSET(0)].code AS med_code
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.medication_request` mr
    WHERE mr.subject.patientId IN (SELECT patientId FROM patients_single_cond)
      AND mr.status = 'active'
      AND mr.medication.codeableConcept IS NOT NULL
      AND mr.medication.codeableConcept.coding[SAFE_OFFSET(0)].code IS NOT NULL
  ),
  patient_drug_count AS (
    SELECT patientId,
           COUNT(DISTINCT med_code) AS drug_count
    FROM patient_drugs
    GROUP BY patientId
  ),

  -- Step 5: For each condition, find the maximum drug count among its patients
  condition_max_drug AS (
    SELECT pc.condition_code,
           pc.condition_display,
           MAX(COALESCE(pdc.drug_count, 0)) AS max_drug_count
    FROM patient_cond pc
    LEFT JOIN patient_drug_count pdc
      ON pc.patientId = pdc.patientId
    GROUP BY pc.condition_code, pc.condition_display
  ),

  -- Step 6: Rank conditions and pick top 8
  ranked AS (
    SELECT condition_code,
           condition_display,
           max_drug_count,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY max_drug_count DESC, condition_code) AS rnk
    FROM condition_max_drug
  )
SELECT condition_code, condition_display, max_drug_count
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk <= 8
ORDER BY max_drug_count DESC, condition_code;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Query to find photographs from the Photographs department with end date 1839 or earlier
-- by known artists, including their titles, artist names, mediums, and image URLs

WITH relevant_objects AS (
    -- First, filter objects based on all the criteria
    SELECT 
        o.object_id,
        o.title,
        o.artist_display_name AS artist_name,
        o.medium,
        o.object_end_date
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects` o
    WHERE 1=1
        -- Object name contains 'Photograph' (case-insensitive)
        AND LOWER(o.object_name) LIKE '%photograph%'
        -- Department is 'Photographs'
        AND o.department = 'Photographs'
        -- Artist is not unknown (not null and doesn't contain 'unknown')
        AND o.artist_display_name IS NOT NULL
        AND LOWER(o.artist_display_name) NOT LIKE '%unknown%'
        -- Object end date is 1839 or earlier
        AND o.object_end_date <= 1839
)
-- Join with images table to get original image URLs
SELECT 
    ro.title,
    ro.artist_name,
    ro.medium,
    i.original_image_url
FROM relevant_objects ro
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.the_met.images` i
    ON ro.object_id = i.object_id
-- Order results by title for consistency
ORDER BY ro.title;
```
</details>

```sql
    WHERE n."id" = '8a78ef2d-d5f7-4d2d-9b47-5adb25cbd373'
      AND n."body" IS NOT NULL
      AND LOWER(f."VALUE") NOT IN (SELECT LOWER(s."VALUE") 
                                   FROM stopwords, LATERAL FLATTEN(INPUT => "sw") s)
),
-- Tokenize all articles but keep only words present in target_tokens
tokenized_articles AS (
    SELECT 
        n."id" AS "article_id",
        LOWER(f."VALUE") AS "word"
    FROM "WORD_VECTORS_US"."WORD_VECTORS_US"."NATURE" n,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(INPUT => REGEXP_EXTRACT_ALL(
                                REGEXP_REPLACE(n."body", '�|''s(\\W)', '\\1'),
                                '(\\d+(,\\d+)*(\\.\\d+)?|[a-zA-Z0-9_]+)'
                            )) f
    WHERE n."body" IS NOT NULL
      AND LOWER(f."VALUE") IN (SELECT "word" FROM target_tokens)
),
-- Join with frequencies and vectors (inner join to keep only words with both)
word_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        ta."article_id",
        ta."word",
        wf."frequency",
        gv."vector"
    FROM tokenized_articles ta
    INNER JOIN "WORD_VECTORS_US"."WORD_VECTORS_US"."WORD_FREQUENCIES" wf
        ON ta."word" = LOWER(wf."word")
    INNER JOIN "WORD_VECTORS_US"."WORD_VECTORS_US"."GLOVE_VECTORS" gv
        ON ta."word" = LOWER(gv."word")
),
-- Flatten vectors and weight each element
weighted_elements AS (
    SELECT 
        ws."article_id",
        f."INDEX" AS "elem_idx",
        f."VALUE"::FLOAT / POWER(ws."frequency", 0.4) AS "weighted_val"
    FROM word_stats ws,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(INPUT => ws."vector") f
),
-- Sum weighted elements per article and index
aggregate_vec AS (
    SELECT 
        "article_id",
        "elem_idx",
        SUM("weighted_val") AS "sum_val"
    FROM weighted_elements
    GROUP BY "article_id", "elem_idx"
),
-- Compute L2 norm for each article vector
article_norms AS (
    SELECT 
        "article_id",
        SQRT(SUM(POWER("sum_val", 2))) AS "norm"
    FROM aggregate_vec
    GROUP BY "article_id"
),
-- Normalize each aggregate vector to unit length
normalized_vec AS (
    SELECT 
        a."article_id",
        a."elem_idx",
        a."sum_val" / n."norm" AS "unit_val"
    FROM aggregate_vec a
    INNER JOIN article_norms n ON a."article_id" = n."article_id"
),
-- Isolate normalized vector of the target article
target_vec AS (
    SELECT 
        "elem_idx",
        "unit_val" AS "target_val"
    FROM normalized_vec
    WHERE "article_id" = '8a78ef2d-d5f7-4d2d-9b47-5adb25cbd373'
),
-- Compute cosine similarity (dot product) between target and all others
article_similarities AS (
    SELECT 
        nv."article_id",
        SUM(nv."unit_val" * tv."target_val") AS "cosine_similarity"
    FROM normalized_vec nv
    INNER JOIN target_vec tv ON nv."elem_idx" = tv."elem_idx"
    WHERE nv."article_id" != '8a78ef2d-d5f7-4d2d-9b47-5adb25cbd373'
    GROUP BY nv."article_id"
)
-- Final output: top 10 most similar articles with metadata
SELECT 
    n."id" AS "article_id",
    n."date",
    n."title",
    ROUND(asim."cosine_similarity", 4) AS "similarity_score"
FROM article_similarities asim
INNER JOIN "WORD_VECTORS_US"."WORD_VECTORS_US"."NATURE" n
    ON asim."article_id" = n."id"
ORDER BY asim."cosine_similarity" DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Find the user with the highest total number of records (interpreted as "clicks") across all photo collection tables.
-- Step 1: Union all photo collection tables (v0_1, v0_2, v0_3) to get all records with user.
-- Step 2: Count records per user, order descending, and limit to 1 to get the top user.

WITH all_photos AS (
  SELECT user
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.eclipse_megamovie.photos_v_0_1`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT user
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.eclipse_megamovie.photos_v_0_2`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT user
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.eclipse_megamovie.photos_v_0_3`
)
SELECT
  user,
  COUNT(*) AS total_clicks
FROM all_photos
GROUP BY user
ORDER BY total_clicks DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH all_pollutants AS (
  -- PM10
  SELECT 'PM10' AS pollutant, date_local, arithmetic_mean
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.pm10_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_name = 'California' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020

  UNION ALL

  -- PM2.5 Federal Reference Method (FRM)
  SELECT 'PM2.5 FRM' AS pollutant, date_local, arithmetic_mean
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.pm25_frm_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_name = 'California' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020

  UNION ALL

  -- PM2.5 Non‑Federal Reference Method (non‑FRM)
  SELECT 'PM2.5 Non-FRM' AS pollutant, date_local, arithmetic_mean
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.pm25_nonfrm_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_name = 'California' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020

  UNION ALL

  -- Volatile organic emissions (VOC)
  SELECT 'VOC' AS pollutant, date_local, arithmetic_mean
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.voc_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_name = 'California' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020

  UNION ALL

  -- Sulfur dioxide (SO₂), scaled by 10
  SELECT 'SO2' AS pollutant, date_local, arithmetic_mean * 10 AS arithmetic_mean
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.so2_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_name = 'California' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020

  UNION ALL

  -- Lead, scaled by 100
  SELECT 'Lead' AS pollutant, date_local, arithmetic_mean * 100 AS arithmetic_mean
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.lead_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_name = 'California' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
),
monthly_avg AS (
  -- Compute monthly average for each pollutant, rounding to 4 decimals
  SELECT
    pollutant,
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(arithmetic_mean), 4) AS avg_value
  FROM all_pollutants
  GROUP BY pollutant, month
)
-- Pivot the monthly averages into a single row per month
SELECT
  month,
  MAX(CASE WHEN pollutant = 'PM10' THEN avg_value END) AS pm10,
  MAX(CASE WHEN pollutant = 'PM2.5 FRM' THEN avg_value END) AS pm25_frm,
  MAX(CASE WHEN pollutant = 'PM2.5 Non-FRM' THEN avg_value END) AS pm25_non_frm,
  MAX(CASE WHEN pollutant = 'VOC' THEN avg_value END) AS volatile_organic_emissions,
  MAX(CASE WHEN pollutant = 'SO2' THEN avg_value END) AS so2_scaled_10,
  MAX(CASE WHEN pollutant = 'Lead' THEN avg_value END) AS lead_scaled_100
FROM monthly_avg
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Get all SOP instances from the specified MR series along with their modality
WITH mr_series_instances AS (
    SELECT
        "SOPInstanceUID",
        "Modality"
    FROM "IDC"."IDC_V17"."DICOM_METADATA"
    WHERE "SeriesInstanceUID" = '1.3.6.1.4.1.14519.5.2.1.3671.4754.105976129314091491952445656147'
),

-- Step 2: Get all segmentation instances that are associated with the MR series
-- Check the SEGMENTATIONS table for the segmented_SeriesInstanceUID
segmentation_instances_from_segmentations AS (
    SELECT
        s."SOPInstanceUID"
    FROM "IDC"."IDC_V17"."SEGMENTATIONS" s
    WHERE s."segmented_SeriesInstanceUID" = '1.3.6.1.4.1.14519.5.2.1.3671.4754.105976129314091491952445656147'
),

-- Step 3: Also check DICOM_METADATA for segmentation instances where SeriesInstanceUID might be in the source image sequence
segmentation_in_dicom AS (
    SELECT
        "SOPInstanceUID",
        "Modality"
    FROM "IDC"."IDC_V17"."DICOM_METADATA"
    WHERE "Modality" IN ('SEG', 'SEGMENTATION')
),

-- Step 4: Try to find segmentations that reference this series through various possible columns
-- First check the segmented_SeriesInstanceUID in SEGMENTATIONS
seg_via_segmentations AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT s."SOPInstanceUID"
    FROM "IDC"."IDC_V17"."SEGMENTATIONS" s
    WHERE s."segmented_SeriesInstanceUID" = '1.3.6.1.4.1.14519.5.2.1.3671.4754.105976129314091491952445656147'
),

-- Step 5: Also check MEASUREMENT_GROUPS which might reference this series
seg_via_measurement_groups AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT m."segmentationInstanceUID" AS "SOPInstanceUID"
    FROM "IDC"."IDC_V17"."MEASUREMENT_GROUPS" m
    WHERE m."sourceSegmentedSeriesUID" = '1.3.6.1.4.1.14519.5.2.1.3671.4754.105976129314091491952445656147'
),

-- Step 6: Combine all possible segmentation SOPInstanceUIDs
all_possible_seg_sops AS (
    SELECT "SOPInstanceUID" FROM seg_via_segmentations
    UNION
    SELECT "SOPInstanceUID" FROM seg_via_measurement_groups
),

-- Step 7: Join with DICOM_METADATA to get modality for segmentation instances
seg_instances_with_modality AS (
    SELECT
        s."SOPInstanceUID",
        COALESCE(d."Modality", 'SEG') AS "Modality"
    FROM all_possible_seg_sops s
    LEFT JOIN "IDC"."IDC_V17"."DICOM_METADATA" d
        ON s."SOPInstanceUID" = d."SOPInstanceUID"
),

-- Step 8: Combine MR series instances with all segmentation instances
combined_instances AS (
    SELECT "SOPInstanceUID", "Modality" FROM mr_series_instances
    UNION
    SELECT "SOPInstanceUID", "Modality" FROM seg_instances_with_modality
)

-- Step 9: Count total SOP instances per modality and find the modality with the highest count
SELECT
    "Modality",
    COUNT(DISTINCT "SOPInstanceUID") AS total_sop_instances
FROM combined_instances
GROUP BY "Modality"
ORDER BY total_sop_instances DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

### 125. sf_bq219 (DB: `IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES`)
**Question**: In the Iowa Liquor Sales dataset, starting from January 1, 2022 through the last fully completed month, which two liquor categories, each contributing an average of at least 1% to the monthly sales volume over at least 24 months of available data, have the lowest Pearson correlation coefficient when comparing their monthly percentages of total liquor sales across those months, and what are their names?

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| CATEGORY1               | CATEGORY2      |
|:------------------------|:---------------|
| AMERICAN FLAVORED VODKA | CREAM LIQUEURS |

**OR**

| output                  |
|:------------------------|
| AMERICAN FLAVORED VODKA |
| CREAM LIQUEURS          |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

| cat_a                   | cat_b          |
|:------------------------|:---------------|
| AMERICAN FLAVORED VODKA | CREAM LIQUEURS |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
N/A
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Determine date range
date_range AS (
    SELECT
        DATE '2022-01-01' AS "start_date",
        DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', MAX("date")) AS "last_month_start"
    FROM "IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."SALES"
    WHERE "date" >= DATE '2022-01-01'
),
-- Step 2: Generate list of all months in range (using existing data months)
months_series AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', "date") AS "month_start"
    FROM "IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."SALES"
    WHERE "date" >= (SELECT "start_date" FROM date_range)
      AND "date" <  (SELECT DATEADD('MONTH', 1, "last_month_start") FROM date_range)
),
-- Step 3: Total monthly sales volume (only months with data)
total_monthly_volume AS (
    SELECT
        DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', "date") AS "month_start",
        SUM("volume_sold_liters") AS "total_volume"
    FROM "IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."SALES"
    WHERE "date" >= (SELECT "start_date" FROM date_range)
      AND "date" <  (SELECT DATEADD('MONTH', 1, "last_month_start") FROM date_range)
    GROUP BY "month_start"
),
-- Step 4: Monthly sales volume per category (including months with zero sales)
category_monthly_volume AS (
    SELECT
        s."category_name",
        DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', s."date") AS "month_start",
        SUM(s."volume_sold_liters") AS "cat_volume"
    FROM "IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."SALES" s
    WHERE s."date" >= (SELECT "start_date" FROM date_range)
      AND s."date" <  (SELECT DATEADD('MONTH', 1, "last_month_start") FROM date_range)
    GROUP BY s."category_name", "month_start"
),
-- Step 5: Build full matrix: every month x every category, with monthly percentage
category_monthly_pct AS (
    SELECT
        m."month_start",
        cat."category_name",
        COALESCE(c."cat_volume", 0) / t."total_volume" AS "monthly_pct"
    FROM months_series m
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT "category_name" FROM category_monthly_volume) cat
    LEFT JOIN category_monthly_volume c
        ON m."month_start" = c."month_start" AND cat."category_name" = c."category_name"
    LEFT JOIN total_monthly_volume t
        ON m."month_start" = t."month_start"
    WHERE t."total_volume" > 0   -- ensure division is safe
),
-- Step 6: Category-level statistics: average percentage and number of months with sales
category_stats AS (
    SELECT
        "category_name",
        AVG("monthly_pct") AS "avg_pct",
        COUNT(CASE WHEN "monthly_pct" > 0 THEN 1 END) AS "months_with_sales"
    FROM category_monthly_pct
    GROUP BY "category_name"
    HAVING "months_with_sales" >= 24 AND "avg_pct" >= 0.01
),
-- Step 7: Filter monthly percentages to only the qualified categories
qualified_monthly_pct AS (
    SELECT mp.*
    FROM category_monthly_pct mp
    INNER JOIN category_stats cs ON mp."category_name" = cs."category_name"
),
-- Step 8: Pairwise Pearson correlation between all qualified categories
pairwise_corr AS (
    SELECT
        a."category_name" AS "cat_a",
        b."category_name" AS "cat_b",
        CORR(a."monthly_pct", b."monthly_pct") AS "pearson_r"
    FROM qualified_monthly_pct a
    INNER JOIN qualified_monthly_pct b
        ON a."month_start" = b."month_start"
       AND a."category_name" < b."category_name"   -- avoid duplicates and self-join
    GROUP BY "cat_a", "cat_b"
)
-- Step 9: Return the pair with the lowest correlation
SELECT "cat_a", "cat_b"
FROM pairwise_corr
ORDER BY "pearson_r" ASC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH

    SELECT
      name,
      SUM(number) AS wy_count
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current`
    WHERE
      gender = 'F'
      AND year = 2021
      AND state = 'WY'
    GROUP BY
      name
  ),
  total_2021 AS (
    SELECT
      name,
      SUM(number) AS total_count
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current`
    WHERE
      gender = 'F'
      AND year = 2021
    GROUP BY
      name
  )
SELECT
  w.name
FROM
  wy_2021 w
  JOIN total_2021 t ON w.name = t.name
WHERE
  t.total_count > 0
ORDER BY
  w.wy_count / t.total_count DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Define cytoband 15q11 coordinates (approximate for hg38)
cytoband AS (
    SELECT
        'chr15' AS "chromosome",
        20000000 AS "start_pos",
        30000000 AS "end_pos"
),

-- Join segment data with cytoband, filter to TCGA-LAML, compute overlap length and copy number
seg_overlap AS (
    SELECT
        seg."case_barcode",
        (seg."major_copy_number" + seg."minor_copy_number") AS "copy_number",
        GREATEST(
            0,
            LEAST(seg."end_pos", cyto."end_pos") - GREATEST(seg."start_pos", cyto."start_pos")
        ) AS "overlap_length"
    FROM "TCGA_MITELMAN"."TCGA_VERSIONED"."COPY_NUMBER_SEGMENT_ALLELIC_HG38_GDC_R23" seg
    JOIN cytoband cyto
        ON seg."chromosome" = cyto."chromosome"
        AND seg."start_pos" < cyto."end_pos"
        AND seg."end_pos" > cyto."start_pos"
    WHERE seg."project_short_name" = 'TCGA-LAML'
),

-- Aggregate per case: weighted average copy number
weighted_avg AS (
    SELECT
        "case_barcode",
        SUM("copy_number" * "overlap_length") / NULLIF(SUM("overlap_length"), 0) AS "weighted_avg_cn"
    FROM seg_overlap
    WHERE "overlap_length" > 0
    GROUP BY "case_barcode"
)

-- Return case barcode with highest weighted average copy number
SELECT
    "case_barcode",
    ROUND("weighted_avg_cn", 4) AS "weighted_avg_copy_number"
FROM weighted_avg
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "weighted_avg_cn" DESC) = 1
ORDER BY "case_barcode";
```
</details>

### 129. sf_bq157 (DB: `PANCANCER_ATLAS_1`)
**Question**: Please compute the T-score to determine the statistical difference in the expression of the DRG2 gene between LGG patients with and without TP53 mutation: for each patient, calculate the average of log10(normalized_count + 1) of DRG2 expression across all their samples, using only samples present in the `MC3_MAF_V5_one_per_tumor_sample` table for the LGG study; identify patients with TP53 mutations from this table where `Hugo_Symbol` is 'TP53' and `FILTER` is 'PASS'; then perform a T-test comparing the mean averaged log-transformed DRG2 expression between patients with and without TP53 mutation.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|   T_SCORE |
|----------:|
|   7.76451 |

**OR**

|   T_SCORE |
|----------:|
|  -7.76451 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|   tscore |
|---------:|
|  -7.7645 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
N/A
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Get distinct LGG samples from MC3 table
lgg_samples AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "Tumor_SampleBarcode" AS "SampleBarcode", "ParticipantBarcode"
    FROM "PANCANCER_ATLAS_1"."PANCANCER_ATLAS_FILTERED"."MC3_MAF_V5_ONE_PER_TUMOR_SAMPLE"
    WHERE "Study" = 'LGG'
),

-- Step 2: Get DRG2 expression for LGG samples that are in MC3, compute log10(normalized_count+1)
expression_data AS (
    SELECT e."ParticipantBarcode", e."SampleBarcode",
           LOG(10, e."normalized_count" + 1) AS "expr_log"
    FROM "PANCANCER_ATLAS_1"."PANCANCER_ATLAS_FILTERED"."EBPP_ADJUSTPANCAN_ILLUMINAHISEQ_RNASEQV2_GENEXP_FILTERED" e
    JOIN lgg_samples s ON e."SampleBarcode" = s."SampleBarcode"
    WHERE e."Study" = 'LGG'
      AND e."Symbol" = 'DRG2'
),

-- Step 3: For each patient, compute average log-expression across all their samples
patient_avg AS (
    SELECT "ParticipantBarcode",
           AVG("expr_log") AS "avg_expr"
    FROM expression_data
    GROUP BY "ParticipantBarcode"
),

-- Step 4: Identify patients with TP53 mutation in LGG (no FILTER column available, omit that condition)
tp53_mut_patients AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "ParticipantBarcode"
    FROM "PANCANCER_ATLAS_1"."PANCANCER_ATLAS_FILTERED"."MC3_MAF_V5_ONE_PER_TUMOR_SAMPLE"
    WHERE "Study" = 'LGG'
      AND "Hugo_Symbol" = 'TP53'
),

-- Step 5: Compute statistics for mutation group (y)
mut_stats AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS "Ny",
           SUM("avg_expr") AS "Sy",
           SUM("avg_expr" * "avg_expr") AS "Qy"
    FROM patient_avg
    WHERE "ParticipantBarcode" IN (SELECT "ParticipantBarcode" FROM tp53_mut_patients)
),

-- Step 6: Compute statistics for all patients (total)
total_stats AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS "Ntotal",
           SUM("avg_expr") AS "Stotal",
           SUM("avg_expr" * "avg_expr") AS "Qtotal"
    FROM patient_avg
)

-- Step 7: Compute T-score (Welch's t-test) using the formula
SELECT 
    ROUND(
        ( "Sy" / "Ny" - ("Stotal" - "Sy") / ("Ntotal" - "Ny") ) 
        / 
        SQRT( 
            ( ("Qy" - "Sy"*"Sy"/"Ny") / ("Ny" - 1) ) / "Ny" +
            ( ( ("Qtotal" - "Qy") - (("Stotal" - "Sy")*("Stotal" - "Sy")/("Ntotal" - "Ny")) ) / ("Ntotal" - "Ny" - 1) ) / ("Ntotal" - "Ny")
        )
    , 4) AS "tscore"
FROM mut_stats, total_stats;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH total_cases AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT "case_barcode") AS "cnt"
    FROM "TCGA_MITELMAN"."TCGA_VERSIONED"."COPY_NUMBER_SEGMENT_ALLELIC_HG38_GDC_R23"
    WHERE "project_short_name" = 'TCGA-KIRC'
),
seg_cytoband AS (
    SELECT
        seg."case_barcode",
        cyto."chromosome",
        cyto."cytoband_name",
        seg."copy_number"
    FROM "TCGA_MITELMAN"."TCGA_VERSIONED"."COPY_NUMBER_SEGMENT_ALLELIC_HG38_GDC_R23" seg
    INNER JOIN "TCGA_MITELMAN"."PROD"."CYTOBANDS_HG38" cyto
        ON seg."chromosome" = cyto."chromosome"
        AND seg."start_pos" < cyto."hg38_stop"
        AND seg."end_pos" > cyto."hg38_start"
    WHERE seg."project_short_name" = 'TCGA-KIRC'
),
max_cn_per_cytoband AS (
    SELECT
        "case_barcode",
        "chromosome",
        "cytoband_name",
        MAX("copy_number") AS "max_cn"
    FROM seg_cytoband
    GROUP BY "case_barcode", "chromosome", "cytoband_name"
),
classified AS (
    SELECT
        "case_barcode",
        "chromosome",
        "cytoband_name",
        CASE
            WHEN "max_cn" > 3 THEN 'Amplification'
            WHEN "max_cn" = 3 THEN 'Gain'
            WHEN "max_cn" = 0 THEN 'Homozygous Deletion'
            WHEN "max_cn" = 1 THEN 'Heterozygous Deletion'
            WHEN "max_cn" = 2 THEN 'Normal'
        END AS "subtype"
    FROM max_cn_per_cytoband
),
counts AS (
    SELECT
        "chromosome",
        "cytoband_name",
        "subtype",
        COUNT(DISTINCT "case_barcode") AS "case_count"
    FROM classified
    GROUP BY "chromosome", "cytoband_name", "subtype"
)
SELECT
    c."chromosome",
    c."cytoband_name",
    c."subtype",
    c."case_count",
    ROUND(c."case_count" * 100.0 / t."cnt", 4) AS "percentage"
FROM counts c
CROSS JOIN total_cases t
ORDER BY
    CASE
        WHEN c."chromosome" = 'chrX' THEN 23
        WHEN c."chromosome" = 'chrY' THEN 24
        ELSE CAST(SUBSTR(c."chromosome", 4) AS INTEGER)
    END,
    c."cytoband_name";
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH sample_allele_counts AS (
    SELECT
        v."start",
        v."end",
        (CAST(c.value:"genotype"[0] AS INTEGER) + CAST(c.value:"genotype"[1] AS INTEGER)) AS alt_alleles,
        sp."Super_Population"
    FROM
        "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."VARIANTS" v,
        LATERAL FLATTEN(input => v."call") c
    INNER JOIN "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."PEDIGREE" ped
        ON CAST(c.value:"call_set_name" AS STRING) = ped."Individual_ID"
    INNER JOIN (
        SELECT DISTINCT "Population", "Super_Population"
        FROM "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."SAMPLE_INFO"
    ) sp
        ON ped."Population" = sp."Population"
    WHERE v."reference_name" = '12'
),

observed_counts AS (
    SELECT
        "start",
        "end",
        SUM(CASE WHEN "Super_Population" = 'EAS' THEN alt_alleles ELSE 0 END) AS a,
        SUM(CASE WHEN "Super_Population" = 'EAS' THEN 2 - alt_alleles ELSE 0 END) AS b,
        SUM(CASE WHEN "Super_Population" != 'EAS' THEN alt_alleles ELSE 0 END) AS c,
        SUM(CASE WHEN "Super_Population" != 'EAS' THEN 2 - alt_alleles ELSE 0 END) AS d,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN "Super_Population" = 'EAS' THEN 1 END) AS n_cases,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN "Super_Population" != 'EAS' THEN 1 END) AS n_controls
    FROM sample_allele_counts
    GROUP BY "start", "end"
),

chi_squared AS (
    SELECT
        "start",
        "end",
        a, b, c, d,
        n_cases,
        n_controls,
        (2 * n_cases * (a + c)) / (a + b + c + d)::FLOAT AS exp_a,
        (2 * n_cases * (b + d)) / (a + b + c + d)::FLOAT AS exp_b,
        (2 * n_controls * (a + c)) / (a + b + c + d)::FLOAT AS exp_c,
        (2 * n_controls * (b + d)) / (a + b + c + d)::FLOAT AS exp_d,
        CASE 
            WHEN (2 * n_cases * (a + c)) / (a + b + c + d)::FLOAT >= 5
             AND (2 * n_cases * (b + d)) / (a + b + c + d)::FLOAT >= 5
             AND (2 * n_controls * (a + c)) / (a + b + c + d)::FLOAT >= 5
             AND (2 * n_controls * (b + d)) / (a + b + c + d)::FLOAT >= 5
            THEN
                POWER(GREATEST(ABS(a - exp_a) - 0.5, 0), 2) / exp_a
                + POWER(GREATEST(ABS(b - exp_b) - 0.5, 0), 2) / exp_b
                + POWER(GREATEST(ABS(c - exp_c) - 0.5, 0), 2) / exp_c
                + POWER(GREATEST(ABS(d - exp_d) - 0.5, 0), 2) / exp_d
            ELSE NULL
        END AS chi_squared_score
    FROM observed_counts
)

SELECT
    "start",
    "end",
    chi_squared_score
FROM chi_squared
WHERE chi_squared_score IS NOT NULL
  AND chi_squared_score >= 29.71679
ORDER BY chi_squared_score DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Filter variants in the region of interest
filtered_variants AS (
    SELECT
        "reference_name",
        "start",
        "end",
        "reference_bases",
        "alternate_bases",
        "VT",
        "HWE",
        "AF",
        "AFR_AF",
        "AMR_AF",
        "EUR_AF",
        "ASN_AF",
        "call"
    FROM
        "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."VARIANTS"
    WHERE
        "reference_name" = '17'
        AND "start" >= 41196311
        AND "end" <= 41277499
),

-- Step 2: Extract distinct alternate bases for each variant
alt_bases AS (
    SELECT
        fv."start",
        fv."end",
        fv."reference_bases",
        ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT f.value::STRING) AS "distinct_alternate_bases"
    FROM
        filtered_variants fv,
        LATERAL FLATTEN(input => fv."alternate_bases") f
    GROUP BY
        fv."start",
        fv."end",
        fv."reference_bases"
),

-- Step 3: Flatten the call array to get individual genotype calls
all_calls AS (
    SELECT
        fv."reference_name",
        fv."start",
        fv."end",
        fv."reference_bases",
        fv."VT",
        fv."HWE",
        fv."AF",
        fv."AFR_AF",
        fv."AMR_AF",
        fv."EUR_AF",
        fv."ASN_AF",
        c.value:"genotype"[0]::INTEGER AS "allele1",
        c.value:"genotype"[1]::INTEGER AS "allele2",
        c.value:"call_set_name"::STRING AS "sample_id"
    FROM
        filtered_variants fv,
        LATERAL FLATTEN(input => fv."call") c
),

-- Step 4: Calculate observed genotype counts per variant
genotype_counts AS (
    SELECT
        "reference_name",
        "start",
        "end",
        "reference_bases",
        "VT",
        "HWE",
        "AF",
        "AFR_AF",
        "AMR_AF",
        "EUR_AF",
        "ASN_AF",
        COUNT(*) AS "total_genotypes",
        SUM(CASE WHEN "allele1" = 0 AND "allele2" = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "obs_hom_ref",
        SUM(CASE WHEN ("allele1" = 0 AND "allele2" = 1) OR ("allele1" = 1 AND "allele2" = 0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "obs_het",
        SUM(CASE WHEN "allele1" = 1 AND "allele2" = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "obs_hom_alt"
    FROM
        all_calls
    GROUP BY
        "reference_name",
        "start",
        "end",
        "reference_bases",
        "VT",
        "HWE",
        "AF",
        "AFR_AF",
        "AMR_AF",
        "EUR_AF",
        "ASN_AF"
),

-- Step 5: Calculate expected counts and chi-squared statistic
hwe_calcs AS (
    SELECT
        gc."reference_name",
        gc."start",
        gc."end",
        gc."reference_bases",
        gc."VT",
        gc."HWE" AS "hwe_from_database",
        gc."AF",
        gc."AFR_AF",
        gc."AMR_AF",
        gc."EUR_AF",
        gc."ASN_AF",
        gc."total_genotypes",
        gc."obs_hom_ref",
        gc."obs_het",
        gc."obs_hom_alt",
        -- Calculate allele frequency of alternate allele from observed counts
        ROUND((2.0 * gc."obs_hom_alt" + gc."obs_het") / (2.0 * gc."total_genotypes"), 6) AS "calc_af",
        -- Expected counts under HWE
        gc."total_genotypes" * POWER(1.0 - ((2.0 * gc."obs_hom_alt" + gc."obs_het") / (2.0 * gc."total_genotypes")), 2) AS "exp_hom_ref",
        gc."total_genotypes" * 2.0 * (1.0 - ((2.0 * gc."obs_hom_alt" + gc."obs_het") / (2.0 * gc."total_genotypes"))) * ((2.0 * gc."obs_hom_alt" + gc."obs_het") / (2.0 * gc."total_genotypes")) AS "exp_het",
        gc."total_genotypes" * POWER(((2.0 * gc."obs_hom_alt" + gc."obs_het") / (2.0 * gc."total_genotypes")), 2) AS "exp_hom_alt",
        -- HWE chi-squared statistic
        ROUND(
            CASE 
                WHEN gc."total_genotypes" > 0 THEN
                    POWER(gc."obs_hom_ref" - gc."total_genotypes" * POWER(1.0 - ((2.0 * gc."obs_hom_alt" + gc."obs_het") / (2.0 * gc."total_genotypes")), 2), 2) / 
                    NULLIF(gc."total_genotypes" * POWER(1.0 - ((2.0 * gc."obs_hom_alt" + gc."obs_het") / (2.0 * gc."total_genotypes")), 2), 0)
                    +
                    POWER(gc."obs_het" - gc."total_genotypes" * 2.0 * (1.0 - ((2.0 * gc."obs_hom_alt" + gc."obs_het") / (2.0 * gc."total_genotypes"))) * ((2.0 * gc."obs_hom_alt" + gc."obs_het") / (2.0 * gc."total_genotypes")), 2) /
                    NULLIF(gc."total_genotypes" * 2.0 * (1.0 - ((2.0 * gc."obs_hom_alt" + gc."obs_het") / (2.0 * gc."total_genotypes"))) * ((2.0 * gc."obs_hom_alt" + gc."obs_het") / (2.0 * gc."total_genotypes")), 0)
                    +
                    POWER(gc."obs_hom_alt" - gc."total_genotypes" * POWER(((2.0 * gc."obs_hom_alt" + gc."obs_het") / (2.0 * gc."total_genotypes")), 2), 2) /
                    NULLIF(gc."total_genotypes" * POWER(((2.0 * gc."obs_hom_alt" + gc."obs_het") / (2.0 * gc."total_genotypes")), 2), 0)
                ELSE NULL
            END, 4
        ) AS "calculated_hwe_chi_squared"
    FROM
        genotype_counts gc
)

-- Final SELECT: return all required columns
SELECT
    hc."reference_name",
    hc."start",
    hc."end",
    hc."reference_bases",
    ab."distinct_alternate_bases",
    hc."VT" AS "variant_type",
    hc."calculated_hwe_chi_squared",
    hc."hwe_from_database",
    hc."total_genotypes",
    hc."obs_hom_ref",
    ROUND(hc."exp_hom_ref", 4) AS "exp_hom_ref",
    hc."obs_het",
    ROUND(hc."exp_het", 4) AS "exp_het",
    hc."obs_hom_alt",
    ROUND(hc."exp_hom_alt", 4) AS "exp_hom_alt",
    hc."AF" AS "overall_allele_frequency",
    hc."AFR_AF" AS "afr_1kg_allele_frequency",
    hc."AMR_AF" AS "amr_1kg_allele_frequency",
    hc."EUR_AF" AS "eur_1kg_allele_frequency",
    hc."ASN_AF" AS "asn_1kg_allele_frequency"
FROM
    hwe_calcs hc
LEFT JOIN
    alt_bases ab
    ON hc."start" = ab."start"
    AND hc."end" = ab."end"
    AND hc."reference_bases" = ab."reference_bases"
ORDER BY
    hc."start",
    hc."reference_bases";
```
</details>

### 133. sf_bq454 (DB: `_1000_GENOMES`)
**Question**: For the 1000 Genomes dataset, analyze common autosomal variants (those with an allele frequency of at least 0.05) across different super populations. For each super population, count how many variants are shared by each specific number of samples within that super population. Include in your results the total population size of each super population, whether the variant is common (allele frequency ≥ 0.05), the number of samples having each variant, and the total count of variants shared by that many samples. Only include autosomal variants by explicitly excluding sex chromosomes (X, Y) and mitochondrial DNA (MT) from the analysis. Consider only samples that have at least one alternate allele (non-reference) for the variant.

```sql
WITH filtered_variants AS (
    SELECT
        v."start",
        v."reference_name",
        v."alternate_bases",
        v."call",
        v."AF"
    FROM "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."VARIANTS" v
    WHERE v."reference_name" NOT IN ('X', 'Y', 'MT')
      AND v."AF" >= 0.05
),

nonref_samples AS (
    SELECT
        fv."start",
        fv."reference_name",
        fv."alternate_bases",
        fv."AF",
        f.value:"call_set_name"::STRING AS sample_id,
        f.value:"genotype"::ARRAY AS genotype
    FROM filtered_variants fv,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => fv."call") f
    WHERE (f.value:"genotype"[0]::INT != 0 OR f.value:"genotype"[1]::INT != 0)
),

sample_superpop AS (
    SELECT
        ns."start",
        ns."reference_name",
        ns."alternate_bases",
        ns."AF",
        ns.sample_id,
        si."Super_Population" AS super_population
    FROM nonref_samples ns
    JOIN "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."SAMPLE_INFO" si
      ON ns.sample_id = si."Sample"
),

variant_sample_counts AS (
    SELECT
        ss."start",
        ss."reference_name",
        ss."alternate_bases",
        ss."AF",
        ss.super_population,
        COUNT(*) AS sample_count
    FROM sample_superpop ss
    GROUP BY
        ss."start",
        ss."reference_name",
        ss."alternate_bases",
        ss."AF",
        ss.super_population
),

variant_count_by_sample_count AS (
    SELECT
        vsc.super_population,
        vsc.sample_count,
        COUNT(*) AS variant_count
    FROM variant_sample_counts vsc
    GROUP BY vsc.super_population, vsc.sample_count
),

pop_size AS (
    SELECT
        "Super_Population",
        COUNT(DISTINCT "Sample") AS total_population_size
    FROM "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."SAMPLE_INFO"
    GROUP BY "Super_Population"
)

SELECT
    vc.super_population,
    ps.total_population_size,
    TRUE AS is_common,
    vc.sample_count AS number_of_samples_having_variant,
    vc.variant_count AS total_count_of_variants_shared_by_that_many_samples
FROM variant_count_by_sample_count vc
JOIN pop_size ps
  ON vc.super_population = ps."Super_Population"
ORDER BY
    vc.super_population,
    vc.sample_count;
```
</details>

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify active stations (status = 'active') with their council district
-- Step 2: Join trips with start and end stations, requiring both stations to be active
-- Step 3: Filter for trips where start and end stations are in the same council district but different stations
-- Step 4: Count trips per council district and return the district with the highest count

WITH active_stations AS (
  SELECT station_id, council_district
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_stations`
  WHERE status = 'active'                -- Consider only active stations
    AND council_district IS NOT NULL     -- Exclude stations without a council district
)

SELECT 
  s_start.council_district AS active_council_district
FROM `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips` t
JOIN active_stations s_start
  ON t.start_station_id = s_start.station_id
JOIN active_stations s_end
  ON SAFE_CAST(t.end_station_id AS INT64) = s_end.station_id
WHERE 
  s_start.council_district = s_end.council_district   -- Same district
  AND t.start_station_id != SAFE_CAST(t.end_station_id AS INT64)  -- Different stations
GROUP BY s_start.council_district
ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
N/A
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH daily_counts AS (
  -- Step 1: Count PUBLIC INTOXICATION incidents per day in 2016
  SELECT 
    date,
    COUNT(*) AS incident_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.austin_incidents.incidents_2016`
  WHERE LOWER(descript) LIKE '%public%intoxication%'
  GROUP BY date
),
z_scores AS (
  -- Step 2: Calculate Z-score for each day
  SELECT 
    date,
    incident_count,
    (incident_count - AVG(incident_count) OVER()) / NULLIF(STDDEV(incident_count) OVER(), 0) AS z_score
  FROM daily_counts
)
-- Step 3: Find second highest Z-score date
SELECT FORMAT_DATE('2016-%m-%d', date) AS date
FROM z_scores
ORDER BY z_score DESC
LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
N/A
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify active stations
WITH active_stations AS (
    SELECT 
        "station_id"
    FROM "AUSTIN"."AUSTIN_BIKESHARE"."BIKESHARE_STATIONS"
    WHERE LOWER("status") = 'active'
),

-- Step 2: Aggregate trips per active station
station_trip_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        t."start_station_id" AS "station_id",
        COUNT(*) AS "total_trips",
        AVG(t."duration_minutes") AS "avg_duration_minutes"
    FROM "AUSTIN"."AUSTIN_BIKESHARE"."BIKESHARE_TRIPS" t
    INNER JOIN active_stations s
        ON t."start_station_id" = s."station_id"
    GROUP BY t."start_station_id"
),

-- Step 3: Overall total trips from active stations
overall_total AS (
    SELECT SUM("total_trips") AS "grand_total"
    FROM station_trip_stats
),

-- Step 4: Rank stations by total trips
ranked_stations AS (
    SELECT 
        "station_id",
        "total_trips",
        "avg_duration_minutes",
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY "total_trips" DESC) AS "rank"
    FROM station_trip_stats
)

-- Step 5: Final selection with percentage and ranking filter
SELECT 
    rs."station_id",
    rs."total_trips",
    ROUND(rs."total_trips" * 100.0 / ot."grand_total", 4) AS "percentage",
    rs."avg_duration_minutes"
FROM ranked_stations rs
CROSS JOIN overall_total ot
WHERE rs."rank" <= 15
ORDER BY rs."rank";
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute total number of articles per category

  SELECT
    category,
    COUNT(*) AS total_articles
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.bbc_news.fulltext`
  GROUP BY category
),

-- Step 2: Compute number of articles that mention "education" per category
education_mentions AS (
  SELECT
    category,
    COUNT(*) AS edu_articles
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.bbc_news.fulltext`
  WHERE LOWER(title) LIKE '%education%'
     OR LOWER(body) LIKE '%education%'
  GROUP BY category
)

-- Step 3: Join the two CTEs and compute the percentage
SELECT
  c.category,
  c.total_articles,
  ROUND(COALESCE(e.edu_articles, 0) * 100.0 / c.total_articles, 4) AS percentage_education
FROM category_counts c
LEFT JOIN education_mentions e
  ON c.category = e.category
ORDER BY c.category;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH filtered_ads AS (
    -- Filter for image-type, Health topic, verified Cyprus advertiser
    -- and ensure all targeting methods are used
    SELECT 
        cs."creative_page_url",
        cs."region_stats",
        cs."creative_id"
    FROM "GOOGLE_ADS"."GOOGLE_ADS_TRANSPARENCY_CENTER"."CREATIVE_STATS" cs
    WHERE cs."ad_format_type" = 'IMAGE'
      AND cs."topic" = 'Health'
      AND cs."advertiser_verification_status" = 'VERIFIED'
      AND cs."advertiser_location" = 'CY'
      -- All targeting methods must be included/excluded, none unused
      AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"demographic_info"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
      AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"geo_location"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
      AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"contextual_signals"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
      AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"customer_lists"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
      AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"topics_of_interest"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
),
croatia_entries AS (
    -- Unpack region_stats to focus on Croatia (HR) entries
    SELECT 
        fa."creative_page_url",
        region.value:"first_shown"::DATE AS "first_shown",
        region.value:"last_shown"::DATE AS "last_shown",
        region.value:"times_shown_availability_date"::DATE AS "times_shown_availability_date",
        region.value:"times_shown_upper_bound"::NUMBER AS "times_shown_upper_bound"
    FROM filtered_ads fa,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => fa."region_stats") region
    WHERE region.value:"region_code"::TEXT = 'HR'
)
-- Select the ad with highest upper bound among those meeting all Croatia criteria
SELECT 
    ce."creative_page_url" AS "creative_page_url"
FROM croatia_entries ce
WHERE ce."times_shown_availability_date" IS NULL
  AND ce."first_shown" > '2023-01-01'
  AND ce."last_shown" < '2024-01-01'
ORDER BY ce."times_shown_upper_bound" DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql

```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Filter instances at the row level
filtered_instances AS (
    SELECT
        "SeriesInstanceUID",
        "SeriesNumber",
        "PatientID",
        "instance_size",           -- assumed column (file size in bytes)
        "ImageType",
        "TransferSyntaxUID",
        "ImageOrientationPatient",
        "ImagePositionPatient",
        "PixelSpacing",
        "Rows",
        "Columns",
        "CTExposureSequence",
        "collection_id"
    FROM "IDC"."IDC_V17"."DICOM_ALL"
    WHERE
        "SOPClassUID" = '1.2.840.10008.5.1.4.1.1.2'  -- CT Image Storage
        AND "collection_id" != 'nlst'
        AND "TransferSyntaxUID" NOT IN ('1.2.840.10008.1.2.4.70', '1.2.840.10008.1.2.4.51')
        AND NOT ARRAY_CONTAINS('LOCALIZER'::VARIANT, "ImageType")
),

-- Step 2: Extract numeric values from VARIANT columns, compute z-axis cross product, and prepare ordering for slice interval check
instance_details AS (
    SELECT
        "SeriesInstanceUID",
        "SeriesNumber",
        "PatientID",
        "instance_size",
        -- ImageOrientationPatient: [x_x, x_y, x_z, y_x, y_y, y_z]
        "ImageOrientationPatient"[0]::FLOAT AS iop_x_x,
        "ImageOrientationPatient"[1]::FLOAT AS iop_x_y,
        "ImageOrientationPatient"[2]::FLOAT AS iop_x_z,
        "ImageOrientationPatient"[3]::FLOAT AS iop_y_x,
        "ImageOrientationPatient"[4]::FLOAT AS iop_y_y,
        "ImageOrientationPatient"[5]::FLOAT AS iop_y_z,
        -- Cross product z component = x_x * y_y - x_y * y_x
        ("ImageOrientationPatient"[0]::FLOAT * "ImageOrientationPatient"[4]::FLOAT -
         "ImageOrientationPatient"[1]::FLOAT * "ImageOrientationPatient"[3]::FLOAT) AS z_cross_component,
        -- ImagePositionPatient: [x, y, z]
        "ImagePositionPatient"[0]::FLOAT AS pos_x,
        "ImagePositionPatient"[1]::FLOAT AS pos_y,
        "ImagePositionPatient"[2]::FLOAT AS pos_z,
        -- PixelSpacing (first element, usually row spacing)
        "PixelSpacing"[0]::FLOAT AS pixel_spacing_row,
        "Rows"::NUMBER AS rows_val,
        "Columns"::NUMBER AS cols_val,
        "CTExposureSequence"::VARCHAR AS ctexposure_str,
        "ImageType"::VARCHAR AS imagetype_str,
        "PixelSpacing"::VARCHAR AS pixelspacing_str
    FROM filtered_instances
),

-- Step 3: For each series, compute ordering by z and derive slice intervals
ordered_instances AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        LAG(pos_z) OVER (PARTITION BY "SeriesInstanceUID" ORDER BY pos_z) AS prev_z,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "SeriesInstanceUID" ORDER BY pos_z) AS rn
    FROM instance_details
),

-- Step 4: Aggregate at series level
series_aggregates AS (
    SELECT
        "SeriesInstanceUID",
        "SeriesNumber",
        "PatientID",
        -- Series size in MiB
        SUM("instance_size") / 1048576.0 AS series_size_mib,
        -- Number of images (instances) in the series
        COUNT(*) AS num_images,
        -- Unique z-positions count
        COUNT(DISTINCT pos_z) AS unique_z_positions,
        -- Check consistency of image orientation (unique value)
        COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(iop_x_x, iop_x_y, iop_x_z, iop_y_x, iop_y_y, iop_y_z)) AS distinct_orientations,
        -- Unique xy positions (must be exactly one)
        COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(pos_x, pos_y)) AS distinct_xy_positions,
        -- Unique pixel spacing
        COUNT(DISTINCT pixelspacing_str) AS distinct_pixelspacing,
        -- Unique rows
        COUNT(DISTINCT rows_val) AS distinct_rows,
        -- Unique columns
        COUNT(DISTINCT cols_val) AS distinct_cols,
        -- Unique CT exposure sequence (string representation)
        COUNT(DISTINCT ctexposure_str) AS distinct_ctexposure,
        -- Slice interval consistency: all non-null differences equal?
        MIN(CASE WHEN prev_z IS NOT NULL THEN pos_z - prev_z END) AS min_diff,
        MAX(CASE WHEN prev_z IS NOT NULL THEN pos_z - prev_z END) AS max_diff,
        -- Z-axis cross product component (take one value, all same)
        MAX(z_cross_component) AS z_cross_abs
    FROM ordered_instances
    GROUP BY "SeriesInstanceUID", "SeriesNumber", "PatientID"
)

-- Step 5: Apply all series-level conditions and retrieve top 5
SELECT
    "SeriesInstanceUID",
    "SeriesNumber",
    "PatientID",
    ROUND(series_size_mib, 4) AS series_size_mib
FROM series_aggregates
WHERE
    -- No duplicate slices: image count equals unique z positions
    num_images = unique_z_positions
    -- All images have the same orientation
    AND distinct_orientations = 1
    -- All images have the same xy position (i.e., all slices share the same in-plane x,y)
    AND distinct_xy_positions = 1
    -- All images have the same pixel spacing
    AND distinct_pixelspacing = 1
    -- All images have the same number of rows and columns
    AND distinct_rows = 1
    AND distinct_cols = 1
    -- All images have the same CT exposure sequence
    AND distinct_ctexposure = 1
    -- Slice intervals are consistent (min_diff = max_diff) and positive
    AND min_diff IS NOT NULL
    AND min_diff = max_diff
    AND min_diff > 0
    -- Z-axis cross product component absolute value between 0.99 and 1.01
    AND ABS(z_cross_abs) BETWEEN 0.99 AND 1.01
ORDER BY series_size_mib DESC
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Filter dicom_all for StudyDate in 2001 and get necessary columns
WITH filtered_dicom AS (
    SELECT
        "PatientID",
        "StudyInstanceUID",
        "StudyDate",
        "SOPInstanceUID"
    FROM "IDC"."IDC_V17"."DICOM_ALL"
    WHERE YEAR("StudyDate") = 2001
),

-- Step 2: Join with quantitative_measurements and extract fields
measurements_with_site AS (
    SELECT
        fd."PatientID",
        fd."StudyInstanceUID",
        fd."StudyDate",
        fd."SOPInstanceUID",
        qm."segmentationInstanceUID",
        qm."Value",
        -- Extract CodeMeaning from Quantity (a VARIANT)
        qm."Quantity":"CodeMeaning"::STRING AS "QuantityCodeMeaning",
        -- Extract CodeMeaning from findingSite (a VARIANT)
        qm."findingSite":"CodeMeaning"::STRING AS "FindingSiteCodeMeaning"
    FROM filtered_dicom fd
    JOIN "IDC"."IDC_V17"."QUANTITATIVE_MEASUREMENTS" qm
        ON fd."SOPInstanceUID" = qm."segmentationInstanceUID"
)

-- Step 3: Filter to the required measurement types and pivot
SELECT
    "PatientID",
    "StudyInstanceUID",
    "StudyDate",
    "FindingSiteCodeMeaning",
    MAX(CASE WHEN LOWER("QuantityCodeMeaning") = LOWER('Elongation') THEN "Value" END) AS "Elongation",
    MAX(CASE WHEN LOWER("QuantityCodeMeaning") = LOWER('Flatness') THEN "Value" END) AS "Flatness",
    MAX(CASE WHEN LOWER("QuantityCodeMeaning") = LOWER('Least Axis in 3D Length') THEN "Value" END) AS "Least_Axis_in_3D_Length",
    MAX(CASE WHEN LOWER("QuantityCodeMeaning") = LOWER('Major Axis in 3D Length') THEN "Value" END) AS "Major_Axis_in_3D_Length",
    MAX(CASE WHEN LOWER("QuantityCodeMeaning") = LOWER('Maximum 3D Diameter of a Mesh') THEN "Value" END) AS "Maximum_3D_Diameter_of_a_Mesh",
    MAX(CASE WHEN LOWER("QuantityCodeMeaning") = LOWER('Minor Axis in 3D Length') THEN "Value" END) AS "Minor_Axis_in_3D_Length",
    MAX(CASE WHEN LOWER("QuantityCodeMeaning") = LOWER('Sphericity') THEN "Value" END) AS "Sphericity",
    MAX(CASE WHEN LOWER("QuantityCodeMeaning") = LOWER('Surface Area of Mesh') THEN "Value" END) AS "Surface_Area_of_Mesh",
    MAX(CASE WHEN LOWER("QuantityCodeMeaning") = LOWER('Surface to Volume Ratio') THEN "Value" END) AS "Surface_to_Volume_Ratio",
    MAX(CASE WHEN LOWER("QuantityCodeMeaning") = LOWER('Volume from Voxel Summation') THEN "Value" END) AS "Volume_from_Voxel_Summation",
    MAX(CASE WHEN LOWER("QuantityCodeMeaning") = LOWER('Volume of Mesh') THEN "Value" END) AS "Volume_of_Mesh"
FROM measurements_with_site
WHERE LOWER("QuantityCodeMeaning") IN (
    LOWER('Elongation'),
    LOWER('Flatness'),
    LOWER('Least Axis in 3D Length'),
    LOWER('Major Axis in 3D Length'),
    LOWER('Maximum 3D Diameter of a Mesh'),
    LOWER('Minor Axis in 3D Length'),
    LOWER('Sphericity'),
    LOWER('Surface Area of Mesh'),
    LOWER('Surface to Volume Ratio'),
    LOWER('Volume from Voxel Summation'),
    LOWER('Volume of Mesh')
)
GROUP BY
    "PatientID",
    "StudyInstanceUID",
    "StudyDate",
    "FindingSiteCodeMeaning"
ORDER BY
    "PatientID",
    "StudyInstanceUID",
    "StudyDate",
    "FindingSiteCodeMeaning";
```

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
N/A
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Get Colorado ZIP code geometries
WITH co_zip AS (
  SELECT zip_code, zip_code_geom
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes`
  WHERE state_code = 'CO'
),

-- Step 2: Get Colorado block group geometries (state name 'Colorado')
co_bg AS (
  SELECT geo_id, blockgroup_geom
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_census_blockgroups.us_blockgroups_national`
  WHERE state_name = 'Colorado'
),

-- Step 3: Count bank branches per ZIP code in Colorado
bank_counts AS (
  SELECT zip_code, COUNT(*) AS bank_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fdic_banks.locations`
  WHERE state = 'CO'
  GROUP BY zip_code
),

-- Step 4: Spatial join to find overlapping areas and compute overlap ratio
spatial_join AS (
  SELECT 
    z.zip_code,
    bg.geo_id,
    ST_AREA(ST_INTERSECTION(z.zip_code_geom, bg.blockgroup_geom)) AS intersection_area,
    ST_AREA(bg.blockgroup_geom) AS bg_area
  FROM co_zip z
  INNER JOIN co_bg bg
    ON ST_INTERSECTS(z.zip_code_geom, bg.blockgroup_geom)
),

-- Step 5: Distribute bank counts to block groups proportionally
weighted AS (
  SELECT 
    sj.zip_code,
    sj.geo_id,
    bc.bank_count * (sj.intersection_area / NULLIF(sj.bg_area, 0)) AS weighted_banks
  FROM spatial_join sj
  JOIN bank_counts bc ON sj.zip_code = bc.zip_code
),

-- Step 6: For each ZIP code, find the maximum weighted banks per block group (concentration)
per_zip_max AS (
  SELECT 
    zip_code,
    MAX(weighted_banks) AS max_banks_per_blockgroup
  FROM weighted
  GROUP BY zip_code
)

-- Final: the ZIP code with the highest concentration
SELECT zip_code, max_banks_per_blockgroup
FROM per_zip_max
ORDER BY max_banks_per_blockgroup DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
N/A
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify the top 5 minor crime categories based on total crimes in 2008
WITH top5_categories AS (
  SELECT 
    minor_category,
    SUM(value) AS total_2008
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
  WHERE year = 2008
  GROUP BY minor_category
  ORDER BY total_2008 DESC
  LIMIT 5
),

-- Step 2: Compute total crimes per year (all categories)
yearly_totals AS (
  SELECT 
    year,
    SUM(value) AS total_crimes
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
  WHERE year >= 2008  -- From 2008 onward as per question
  GROUP BY year
),

-- Step 3: Compute sum per year for each of the top 5 categories
yearly_category_sums AS (
  SELECT 
    c.year,
    c.minor_category,
    SUM(c.value) AS category_sum
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa` c
  INNER JOIN top5_categories t ON c.minor_category = t.minor_category
  WHERE c.year >= 2008
  GROUP BY c.year, c.minor_category
)

-- Step 4: Pivot the results and compute percentage shares
SELECT 
  yt.year,
  ROUND(100.0 * MAX(CASE WHEN ycs.minor_category = (SELECT minor_category FROM top5_categories ORDER BY total_2008 DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 0) THEN ycs.category_sum ELSE 0 END) / yt.total_crimes, 2) AS top1_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * MAX(CASE WHEN ycs.minor_category = (SELECT minor_category FROM top5_categories ORDER BY total_2008 DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1) THEN ycs.category_sum ELSE 0 END) / yt.total_crimes, 2) AS top2_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * MAX(CASE WHEN ycs.minor_category = (SELECT minor_category FROM top5_categories ORDER BY total_2008 DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 2) THEN ycs.category_sum ELSE 0 END) / yt.total_crimes, 2) AS top3_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * MAX(CASE WHEN ycs.minor_category = (SELECT minor_category FROM top5_categories ORDER BY total_2008 DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 3) THEN ycs.category_sum ELSE 0 END) / yt.total_crimes, 2) AS top4_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * MAX(CASE WHEN ycs.minor_category = (SELECT minor_category FROM top5_categories ORDER BY total_2008 DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 4) THEN ycs.category_sum ELSE 0 END) / yt.total_crimes, 2) AS top5_pct
FROM yearly_totals yt
LEFT JOIN yearly_category_sums ycs ON yt.year = ycs.year
GROUP BY yt.year, yt.total_crimes
ORDER BY yt.year;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Get all distinct image IDs and their original URLs
WITH images_list AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT image_id, original_url
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.images`
),

-- Step 2: Identify images with cat label at confidence=1
cat_labels AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT image_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.labels`
  WHERE label_name = '/m/01yrx'
    AND confidence = 1.0
),

-- Step 3: Identify images that have any cat label (regardless of confidence)
any_cat_labels AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT image_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.labels`
  WHERE label_name = '/m/01yrx'
)

-- Step 4: Compute two counts
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN cl.image_id IS NOT NULL THEN i.original_url END) AS cat_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN acl.image_id IS NULL THEN i.original_url END) AS other_count
FROM images_list i
LEFT JOIN cat_labels cl ON i.image_id = cl.image_id
LEFT JOIN any_cat_labels acl ON i.image_id = acl.image_id;
```
</details>

### 155. sf_bq371 (DB: `WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS`)
**Question**: In the year 2013, considering each invoice’s total value as the product of unit price and quantity and grouping by the quarter (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4) in which the invoice date occurs, what is the difference between the maximum and minimum average invoice values across these quarters?

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|   DIFFERENCE |
|-------------:|
|       139.02 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|   difference |
|-------------:|
|       139.02 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
N/A
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute total value per invoice from invoice lines in 2013
WITH invoice_totals AS (
    SELECT
        inv."InvoiceID",
        EXTRACT(quarter FROM TO_DATE(inv."InvoiceDate", 'YYYY-MM-DD')) AS "quarter",
        SUM(sil."UnitPrice" * sil."Quantity") AS "total_value"
    FROM WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS.WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS.SALES_INVOICES inv
    JOIN WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS.WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS.SALES_INVOICELINES sil
        ON inv."InvoiceID" = sil."InvoiceID"
    WHERE EXTRACT(year FROM TO_DATE(inv."InvoiceDate", 'YYYY-MM-DD')) = 2013
    GROUP BY inv."InvoiceID", EXTRACT(quarter FROM TO_DATE(inv."InvoiceDate", 'YYYY-MM-DD'))
),
-- Step 2: Compute average invoice total per quarter
quarterly_averages AS (
    SELECT
        "quarter",
        AVG("total_value") AS "avg_invoice_value"
    FROM invoice_totals
    GROUP BY "quarter"
)
-- Step 3: Compute difference between max and min quarterly averages
SELECT
    MAX("avg_invoice_value") - MIN("avg_invoice_value") AS "difference"
FROM quarterly_averages;
```
</details>

### 156. bq393 (DB: `hacker_news`)
**Question**: I want to identify users who had activity followed by inactivity. Specifically, find the user ID and their corresponding month number (counting from their first activity month) for the user with the highest month number who became inactive (no activity recorded) after their last recorded activity month. For this analysis, only consider data up until September 10, 2024, and ensure the month number represents the count of months since the user's first activity. The user should have at least one month where they were expected to be active (within their activity span) but actually had no records.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|:----------|---------------:|
| adamsmith |            216 |

| user_id     |   month_number |
|:------------|---------------:|
| gaborcselle |            216 |

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
N/A
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH activity_months AS (
  SELECT 
    `by` AS user_id,
    DATE_TRUNC(DATE(timestamp), MONTH) AS activity_month
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.hacker_news.full`
  WHERE 
    `by` IS NOT NULL 
    AND `by` != 'None'
    AND (deleted IS NULL OR deleted = FALSE)
    AND (dead IS NULL OR dead = FALSE)
    AND timestamp <= TIMESTAMP('2024-09-10 23:59:59')
  GROUP BY user_id, activity_month
),

user_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    user_id,
    MIN(activity_month) AS first_month,
    MAX(activity_month) AS last_month,
    COUNT(activity_month) AS num_active_months
  FROM activity_months
  GROUP BY user_id
),

inactive_month_candidates AS (
  SELECT 
    user_id,
    first_month,
    last_month,
    num_active_months,
    DATE_ADD(last_month, INTERVAL 1 MONTH) AS inactive_month
  FROM user_stats
  WHERE last_month < DATE('2024-09-01')
),

eligible_users AS (
  SELECT 
    user_id,
    DATE_DIFF(inactive_month, first_month, MONTH) + 1 AS month_number
  FROM inactive_month_candidates
  WHERE num_active_months < DATE_DIFF(last_month, first_month, MONTH) + 1
)

SELECT user_id, month_number
FROM eligible_users
ORDER BY month_number DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

### 157. bq402 (DB: `ecommerce`)
**Question**: Calculate the conversion rate from unique visitors to purchasers by using data exclusively from the `web_analytics` table in the `data-to-insights.ecommerce` dataset. A visitor is defined as a unique `fullVisitorId` present in the table, while a purchaser is a visitor who has at least one transaction recorded (`totals.transactions` is not null). The conversion rate is computed by dividing the number of unique purchasers by the total number of unique visitors. Additionally, calculate the average number of transactions per purchaser, considering only those visitors who have made at least one transaction.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|------------------:|---------------------------------:|
|         0.0269845 |                          1.24412 |

**OR**

|   TOTAL_UNIQUE_VISITORS |   UNIQUE_PURCHASERS |   TOTAL_TRANSACTIONS |   CONVERSION_RATE_PERCENTAGE |   AVG_TRANSACTIONS_PER_PURCHASER |
|------------------------:|--------------------:|---------------------:|-----------------------------:|---------------------------------:|
|                  741721 |               20015 |                24901 |                          2.7 |                             1.24 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|   conversion_rate |   avg_transactions_per_purchaser |
|------------------:|---------------------------------:|
|             0.027 |                           1.2441 |

<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
N/A
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute total unique visitors from the web_analytics table
WITH visitors AS (
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT fullVisitorId) AS total_visitors
  FROM `data-to-insights.ecommerce.web_analytics`
),

-- Step 2: Identify purchasers (visitors with at least one transaction) and sum their transactions
purchasers AS (
  SELECT fullVisitorId,
         SUM(totals.transactions) AS total_transactions
  FROM `data-to-insights.ecommerce.web_analytics`
  WHERE totals.transactions IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY fullVisitorId
),

-- Step 3: Aggregate purchaser-level statistics
purchaser_stats AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_purchasers,
         SUM(total_transactions) AS total_transactions_sum
  FROM purchasers
)

-- Step 4: Calculate conversion rate and average transactions per purchaser
SELECT
  ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(purchaser_stats.num_purchasers, visitors.total_visitors), 4) AS conversion_rate,
  ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(purchaser_stats.total_transactions_sum, purchaser_stats.num_purchasers), 4) AS avg_transactions_per_purchaser
FROM visitors, purchaser_stats;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH 
vote_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        "ToUserId" AS user_id,
        COUNT(*) AS upvote_count
    FROM "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMMESSAGEVOTES"
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "VoteDate") = 2019
    GROUP BY "ToUserId"

    FROM vote_counts
),
differences AS (
    SELECT 
        vc.user_id,
        vc.upvote_count,
        a.avg_upvotes,
        ABS(vc.upvote_count - a.avg_upvotes) AS diff
    FROM vote_counts vc
    CROSS JOIN average a
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        d.user_id,
        d.upvote_count,
        d.diff,
        u."UserName",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY d.diff ASC, u."UserName" ASC) AS rn
    FROM differences d
    JOIN "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."USERS" u ON d.user_id = u."Id"
)
SELECT 
    "UserName",
    user_id
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Filter death records for white individuals (RaceRecode3 = 1) and join with ICD-10 code descriptions
WITH white_deaths AS (
    SELECT
        dr."Icd10Code",
        dr."AgeRecode12",
        ic."Description"
    FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."DEATHRECORDS" dr
    JOIN "DEATH"."DEATH"."ICD10CODE" ic
        ON dr."Icd10Code" = ic."Code"
    WHERE dr."RaceRecode3" = 1
),

-- Step 2: Classify each death into 'discharge' or 'vehicle' based on description,
-- excluding the three specific discharge descriptions
classified AS (
    SELECT
        "AgeRecode12",
        "Icd10Code",
        "Description",
        CASE
            WHEN LOWER("Description") LIKE '%discharge%'
                 AND "Description" NOT IN (
                     'Urethral discharge',
                     'Discharge of firework',
                     'Legal intervention involving firearm discharge'
                 )
            THEN 'discharge'
            WHEN LOWER("Description") LIKE '%vehicle%'
            THEN 'vehicle'
            ELSE NULL
        END AS category
    FROM white_deaths
    WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%discharge%'
       OR LOWER("Description") LIKE '%vehicle%'
),

-- Step 3: Count deaths per ICD-10 code, per age group, per category
death_counts AS (
    SELECT
        "AgeRecode12",
        "Icd10Code",
        category,
        COUNT(*) AS death_count
    FROM classified
    WHERE category IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY "AgeRecode12", "Icd10Code", category
),

-- Step 4: Average death count per code for each age group and category
avg_by_group AS (
    SELECT
        "AgeRecode12",
        category,
        AVG(death_count) AS avg_deaths_per_code
    FROM death_counts
    GROUP BY "AgeRecode12", category
),

-- Step 5: Pivot to get separate columns for discharge and vehicle averages
pivoted AS (
    SELECT
        a."AgeRecode12",
        MAX(CASE WHEN a.category = 'discharge' THEN a.avg_deaths_per_code ELSE NULL END) AS avg_discharge,
        MAX(CASE WHEN a.category = 'vehicle'   THEN a.avg_deaths_per_code ELSE NULL END) AS avg_vehicle
    FROM avg_by_group a
    GROUP BY a."AgeRecode12"
)

-- Step 6: Compute difference (discharge - vehicle) and join with age group description
SELECT
    p."AgeRecode12",
    ag."Description" AS "AgeGroup",
    ROUND(COALESCE(p.avg_discharge, 0) - COALESCE(p.avg_vehicle, 0), 4) AS "difference"
FROM pivoted p
LEFT JOIN "DEATH"."DEATH"."AGERECODE12" ag
    ON p."AgeRecode12" = ag."Code"
ORDER BY p."AgeRecode12";
```
</details>

```sql
  SELECT
    transaction_id,
    item.item_id,
    item.item_name,
    item.quantity
  FROM december_purchases,
  UNNEST(items) AS item
  WHERE item.item_name IS NOT NULL
),
-- Step 3: Identify transaction IDs that contain 'Google Navy Speckled Tee'
transactions_with_tee AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT transaction_id
  FROM purchase_items
  WHERE item_name = 'Google Navy Speckled Tee'
),
-- Step 4: Get all items from those transactions, excluding the tee itself
other_items_in_tee_transactions AS (
  SELECT
    pi.item_id,
    pi.item_name,
    pi.quantity
  FROM purchase_items pi
  INNER JOIN transactions_with_tee twt
    ON pi.transaction_id = twt.transaction_id
  WHERE pi.item_name != 'Google Navy Speckled Tee'
)
-- Step 5: Aggregate total quantity per other product and pick the highest
SELECT
  item_id,
  item_name,
  SUM(quantity) AS total_quantity
FROM other_items_in_tee_transactions
GROUP BY item_id, item_name
ORDER BY total_quantity DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
WITH september_15_events AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM `firebase-public-project.analytics_153293282.events_20180915`
  WHERE event_name = 'level_complete_quickplay'
),

board_scores AS (
  SELECT
    e.user_pseudo_id,
    e.event_timestamp,
    -- Try extracting board_type with possible key names
    COALESCE(
      (SELECT ep.value.string_value 
       FROM UNNEST(e.event_params) ep 
       WHERE ep.key = 'board_type'),
      (SELECT ep.value.string_value 
       FROM UNNEST(e.event_params) ep 
       WHERE ep.key = 'board'),
      (SELECT ep.value.string_value 
       FROM UNNEST(e.event_params) ep 
       WHERE ep.key = 'difficulty'),
      (SELECT ep.value.string_value 
       FROM UNNEST(e.event_params) ep 
       WHERE ep.key = 'level_name')
    ) AS board_type,
    -- Try extracting score from 'value' key (int_value)
    (SELECT ep.value.int_value 
     FROM UNNEST(e.event_params) ep 
     WHERE ep.key = 'value') AS score
  FROM september_15_events e
)

SELECT
  COALESCE(board_type, 'Unknown') AS board_type,
  ROUND(AVG(score), 2) AS average_score,
  COUNT(*) AS number_of_completions
FROM board_scores
WHERE score IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY board_type
ORDER BY average_score DESC NULLS LAST;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Compute the average pageviews per user for purchasers and non-purchasers in December 2020,
-- then calculate the difference (purchaser average minus non-purchaser average).
-- Purchaser is defined as a user with at least one 'purchase' event in December 2020.

WITH user_agg AS (
  SELECT
    user_pseudo_id,
    -- Count total page_view events for the user in December 2020
    COUNTIF(event_name = 'page_view') AS pageviews,
    -- Flag if user ever had a purchase event in December 2020
    LOGICAL_OR(event_name = 'purchase') AS is_purchaser
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20201201' AND '20201231'
    AND user_pseudo_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY user_pseudo_id
)
SELECT
  AVG(CASE WHEN is_purchaser THEN pageviews END) AS avg_purchaser_pageviews,
  AVG(CASE WHEN NOT is_purchaser THEN pageviews END) AS avg_non_purchaser_pageviews,
  AVG(CASE WHEN is_purchaser THEN pageviews END) - 
    AVG(CASE WHEN NOT is_purchaser THEN pageviews END) AS avg_difference
FROM user_agg;
```
</details>

```sql
    (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'page_location') AS page_url
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_202101*`
  WHERE
    event_name = 'page_view'
),

-- Step 2: Count total views per page
page_view_counts AS (
  SELECT
    page_url,
    COUNT(*) AS view_count
  FROM
    page_views
  WHERE
    page_url IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    page_url
),

-- Step 3: Identify the most frequently visited page (highest view count)
most_frequent_page AS (
  SELECT
    page_url
  FROM
    page_view_counts
  ORDER BY
    view_count DESC
  LIMIT 1
)

-- Step 4: Count distinct users who viewed that page in January 2021
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_pseudo_id) AS distinct_user_count
FROM
  page_views
WHERE
  page_url = (SELECT page_url FROM most_frequent_page);
```

The conversion rate should be calculated as the percentage of user visits that reached both the Home and Checkout Confirmation pages in one session, relative to those that landed on the Home page.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Extract page_view events with page title and session ID from event_params
WITH events_with_params AS (
  SELECT
    user_pseudo_id,
    event_timestamp,
    event_date,
    MAX(CASE WHEN param.key = 'page_title' THEN param.value.string_value END) AS page_title,
    MAX(CASE WHEN param.key = 'ga_session_id' THEN param.value.int_value END) AS session_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_20210102`
  CROSS JOIN UNNEST(event_params) AS param
  WHERE event_name = 'page_view'
    AND event_date = '20210102'  -- ensure date filter, though table is for that date
  GROUP BY user_pseudo_id, event_timestamp, event_date
),

-- Step 2: Rank events within each session (user_pseudo_id + session_id) by timestamp
session_events AS (
  SELECT
    user_pseudo_id,
    session_id,
    event_timestamp,
    page_title,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY user_pseudo_id, session_id
      ORDER BY event_timestamp
    ) AS event_rank
  FROM events_with_params
  WHERE session_id IS NOT NULL  -- exclude sessions without a session ID
),

-- Step 3: Mark sessions that started with Home page as landing sessions
-- and check if they also contain a Checkout Confirmation page view
session_analysis AS (
  SELECT
    user_pseudo_id,
    session_id,
    MAX(CASE WHEN event_rank = 1 AND page_title = 'Home' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS is_landing_home,
    MAX(CASE WHEN page_title = 'Checkout Confirmation' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_checkout_confirmation
  FROM session_events
  GROUP BY user_pseudo_id, session_id
)

-- Step 4: Calculate conversion rate
SELECT
  SAFE_DIVIDE(
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN is_landing_home = 1 AND has_checkout_confirmation = 1 THEN CONCAT(user_pseudo_id, session_id) END),
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN is_landing_home = 1 THEN CONCAT(user_pseudo_id, session_id) END)
  ) * 100 AS conversion_rate_percentage
FROM session_analysis;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Extract purchase events with valid revenue and session ID
WITH purchase_sessions AS (
    SELECT
        user_pseudo_id,
        -- Extract ga_session_id from event_params, handling both string and int values
        COALESCE(
            (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'ga_session_id'),
            CAST((SELECT value.int_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'ga_session_id') AS STRING)
        ) AS ga_session_id,
        ecommerce.purchase_revenue_in_usd AS revenue_usd
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*`
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20201101' AND '20201130'
        AND event_name = 'purchase'
        AND ecommerce.purchase_revenue_in_usd IS NOT NULL
        -- Ensure session ID is not null (either string or int)
        AND (
            (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'ga_session_id') IS NOT NULL
            OR (SELECT value.int_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'ga_session_id') IS NOT NULL
        )
),

-- Step 2: Compute total revenue per session (sum of purchase revenues)
session_revenue AS (
    SELECT
        user_pseudo_id,
        ga_session_id,
        SUM(revenue_usd) AS total_revenue_per_session
    FROM purchase_sessions
    WHERE ga_session_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY user_pseudo_id, ga_session_id
),

-- Step 3: Identify users with more than one purchase session
users_with_multiple_sessions AS (
    SELECT
        user_pseudo_id
    FROM session_revenue
    GROUP BY user_pseudo_id
    HAVING COUNT(ga_session_id) > 1
)

-- Step 4: Final output � average purchase revenue per session per user
SELECT
    u.user_pseudo_id,
    ROUND(AVG(u.total_revenue_per_session), 4) AS avg_purchase_revenue_usd_per_session
FROM session_revenue u
INNER JOIN users_with_multiple_sessions m
    ON u.user_pseudo_id = m.user_pseudo_id
GROUP BY u.user_pseudo_id
ORDER BY avg_purchase_revenue_usd_per_session DESC NULLS LAST;
```
</details>
