```sql
-- Step 1: Extract page_view events from all December 2020 tables
WITH page_views AS (
  SELECT
    event_timestamp,
    event_params,
    event_dimensions
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_202012*`
  WHERE event_name = 'page_view'
),

-- Step 2: Unnest event_params to get the page_location URL
page_locations AS (
  SELECT
    pv.event_timestamp,
    (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(pv.event_params) WHERE key = 'page_location') AS page_location
  FROM page_views pv
),

-- Step 3: Filter to the target website, extract the path, and clean extra slashes
clean_paths AS (
  SELECT
    REGEXP_REPLACE(
      REGEXP_EXTRACT(page_location, r'^https?://[^/]+(/[^?#]*)'),  -- extract path after domain
      r'//+',                                                       -- replace multiple consecutive slashes with one
      '/'
    ) AS cleaned_path
  FROM page_locations
  WHERE page_location IS NOT NULL
    AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(page_location, r'^https?://shop\.googlemerchandisestore\.com')
)

-- Step 4: Count page views per cleaned path, rank, and return the second highest
SELECT
  cleaned_path,
  COUNT(*) AS total_page_views
FROM clean_paths
GROUP BY cleaned_path
ORDER BY total_page_views DESC, cleaned_path ASC  -- deterministic tie-breaking
LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Define a CTE for purchase events on 2020-11-30 with computed tax rate
WITH purchase_events AS (
  SELECT
    ecommerce.transaction_id,
    ecommerce.total_item_quantity,
    ecommerce.purchase_revenue_in_usd,
    ecommerce.purchase_revenue,
    ecommerce.tax_value_in_usd,
    -- Compute tax rate: tax_value_in_usd / purchase_revenue_in_usd, avoid division by zero
    SAFE_DIVIDE(ecommerce.tax_value_in_usd, ecommerce.purchase_revenue_in_usd) AS tax_rate,
    -- Flatten the items array to get each item's category
    items
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_20201130`
  CROSS JOIN UNNEST(items) AS items
  WHERE event_name = 'purchase'
    AND ecommerce.transaction_id IS NOT NULL
    AND ecommerce.purchase_revenue_in_usd > 0
),

-- Step 2: Compute average tax rate per item category across all purchase events
category_avg_tax AS (
  SELECT
    items.item_category,
    AVG(tax_rate) AS avg_tax_rate
  FROM purchase_events
  -- Exclude null or empty categories
  WHERE items.item_category IS NOT NULL AND items.item_category != ''
  GROUP BY items.item_category
),

-- Step 3: Identify the item category with the highest average tax rate
top_category AS (
  SELECT item_category
  FROM category_avg_tax
  ORDER BY avg_tax_rate DESC, item_category  -- deterministic tie-break by category name
  LIMIT 1
)

-- Step 4: Retrieve transaction details for purchase events that contain the top category
SELECT DISTINCT
  pe.transaction_id,
  pe.total_item_quantity,
  pe.purchase_revenue_in_usd,
  pe.purchase_revenue
FROM purchase_events pe
-- Join with the top category on the item level
INNER JOIN top_category tc
  ON pe.items.item_category = tc.item_category
ORDER BY pe.transaction_id;
```
</details>

For each group, calculate the retention rate in the fourth week (i.e., the percentage of users from the original group who returned in the fourth week after their first session). Please identify the cohort with the highest retention rate in the fourth week, and name the group by the Monday date of the cohort's first session week. Return the result in the format "YYYY-MM-DD".

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
N/A
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Define all session_start events from available tables (from July 2, 2018 onward)
WITH all_sessions AS (
  SELECT
    user_pseudo_id,
    PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', event_date) AS event_date
  FROM `firebase-public-project.analytics_153293282.events_*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20180702' AND '20181003'
    AND event_name = 'session_start'
),

-- Step 2: Find each user's first session date (on or after July 2, 2018)
first_session AS (
  SELECT
    user_pseudo_id,
    MIN(event_date) AS first_session_date
  FROM all_sessions
  GROUP BY user_pseudo_id
  HAVING first_session_date >= '2018-07-02'
),

-- Step 3: Assign each user to the cohort defined by the Monday of the week of their first session
cohort AS (
  SELECT
    user_pseudo_id,
    first_session_date,
    DATE_TRUNC(first_session_date, WEEK(MONDAY)) AS cohort_week_start
  FROM first_session
),

-- Step 4: Identify users who had a session_start in the 4th week after their cohort Monday
week4_sessions AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    c.user_pseudo_id,
    c.cohort_week_start
  FROM cohort c
  JOIN all_sessions s
    ON c.user_pseudo_id = s.user_pseudo_id
   AND s.event_date >= DATE_ADD(c.cohort_week_start, INTERVAL 21 DAY)  -- Monday of 4th week
   AND s.event_date <  DATE_ADD(c.cohort_week_start, INTERVAL 28 DAY)  -- Monday of 5th week (exclusive)
)

-- Step 5: Aggregate by cohort and calculate retention rate, then find the top cohort
SELECT
  FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', c.cohort_week_start) AS cohort_monday
FROM cohort c
LEFT JOIN week4_sessions w
  ON c.user_pseudo_id = w.user_pseudo_id
GROUP BY c.cohort_week_start
ORDER BY
  SAFE_DIVIDE(COUNT(DISTINCT w.user_pseudo_id), COUNT(DISTINCT c.user_pseudo_id)) DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH
  -- Step 1: Identify users whose first touch was in September 2018
  first_touch_users AS (
    SELECT
      user_pseudo_id,
      DATE(TIMESTAMP_MICROS(MIN(user_first_touch_timestamp))) AS first_touch_date
    FROM
      `firebase-public-project.analytics_153293282.events_*`
    WHERE
      _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20180612' AND '20181003'
      AND user_first_touch_timestamp IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY
      user_pseudo_id
    HAVING
      EXTRACT(YEAR FROM DATE(TIMESTAMP_MICROS(MIN(user_first_touch_timestamp)))) = 2018
      AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM DATE(TIMESTAMP_MICROS(MIN(user_first_touch_timestamp)))) = 9
  ),

  -- Step 2: Find uninstall events within 7 days for those users (app_remove event)
  uninstall_events AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      e.user_pseudo_id,
      DATE(TIMESTAMP_MICROS(e.event_timestamp)) AS uninstall_date
    FROM
      `firebase-public-project.analytics_153293282.events_*` e
      INNER JOIN first_touch_users f ON e.user_pseudo_id = f.user_pseudo_id
    WHERE
      _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20180612' AND '20181003'
      AND e.event_name = 'app_remove'
      AND DATE_DIFF(DATE(TIMESTAMP_MICROS(e.event_timestamp)), f.first_touch_date, DAY) BETWEEN 0 AND 7
  ),

  -- Step 3: Identify users who experienced at least one crash (app_exception event)
  crash_users AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      e.user_pseudo_id
    FROM
      `firebase-public-project.analytics_153293282.events_*` e
      INNER JOIN first_touch_users f ON e.user_pseudo_id = f.user_pseudo_id
    WHERE
      _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20180612' AND '20181003'
      AND e.event_name = 'app_exception'
  )

-- Step 4: Compute the percentage
SELECT
  SAFE_DIVIDE(
    COUNT(DISTINCT cu.user_pseudo_id),
    COUNT(DISTINCT ue.user_pseudo_id)
  ) * 100 AS percentage_crash_within_7d_uninstall
FROM
  (SELECT DISTINCT user_pseudo_id FROM uninstall_events) ue
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT user_pseudo_id FROM crash_users) cu
    ON ue.user_pseudo_id = cu.user_pseudo_id;
```

```sql
    SELECT
        DATE(o."order_purchase_timestamp") AS sale_date,
        SUM(oi."price") AS total_sales
    FROM "orders" o
    JOIN "order_items" oi ON o."order_id" = oi."order_id"
    JOIN "products" p ON oi."product_id" = p."product_id"
    JOIN "product_category_name_translation" t ON p."product_category_name" = t."product_category_name"
    WHERE (LOWER(t."product_category_name_english") LIKE '%toy%'
           OR LOWER(p."product_category_name") LIKE '%brinqued%')
      AND o."order_purchase_timestamp" >= '2017-01-01'
      AND o."order_purchase_timestamp" < '2018-08-30'   -- up to Aug 29 inclusive
    GROUP BY sale_date
),

-- Step 2: Compute regression aggregates (x = days since 2017-01-01, y = sales)
regression_agg AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) AS n,
        SUM(x) AS sum_x,
        SUM(y) AS sum_y,
        SUM(x * y) AS sum_xy,
        SUM(x * x) AS sum_x2
    FROM (
        SELECT
            julianday(sale_date) - julianday('2017-01-01') AS x,
            total_sales AS y
        FROM daily_sales
    )
),

-- Step 3: Calculate slope and intercept (simple linear regression)
regression AS (
    SELECT
        (n * sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y) / (n * sum_x2 - sum_x * sum_x) AS slope,
        (sum_y - ((n * sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y) / (n * sum_x2 - sum_x * sum_x)) * sum_x) / n AS intercept
    FROM regression_agg
),

-- Step 4: Generate dates from Dec 3 to Dec 10, 2018 (needed for symmetric moving average)
pred_dates AS (
    SELECT DATE('2018-12-03') AS pred_date
    UNION ALL
    SELECT DATE(pred_date, '+1 day')
    FROM pred_dates
    WHERE pred_date < DATE('2018-12-10')
),

-- Step 5: Predict sales for each of these dates using the linear model
predicted_sales AS (
    SELECT
        pd.pred_date,
        r.intercept + r.slope * (julianday(pd.pred_date) - julianday('2017-01-01')) AS predicted_sale
    FROM pred_dates pd
    CROSS JOIN regression r
),

-- Step 6: Define the four target dates (Dec 5 to Dec 8)
target_dates AS (
    SELECT DATE('2018-12-05') AS target_date
    UNION ALL
    SELECT DATE('2018-12-06')
    UNION ALL
    SELECT DATE('2018-12-07')
    UNION ALL
    SELECT DATE('2018-12-08')
),

-- Step 7: Compute 5-day symmetric moving average for each target date
moving_averages AS (
    SELECT
        td.target_date,
        (SELECT AVG(ps.predicted_sale)
         FROM predicted_sales ps
         WHERE ps.pred_date BETWEEN DATE(td.target_date, '-2 days') AND DATE(td.target_date, '+2 days')
        ) AS ma
    FROM target_dates td
)

-- Step 8: Sum the four moving averages and round to 4 decimal places
SELECT ROUND(SUM(ma), 4) AS sum_of_moving_averages
FROM moving_averages;
```
</details>

```sql
-- CTE: total payment per order (sum of multiple installments)
WITH "order_payment_totals" AS (
    SELECT
        "order_id",
        SUM("payment_value") AS "payment_total"
    FROM "order_payments"
    GROUP BY "order_id"
),

-- CTE: combine orders with payments and customer unique IDs
"customer_orders" AS (
    SELECT
        "c"."customer_unique_id",
        "o"."order_id",
        "o"."order_purchase_timestamp",
        COALESCE("opt"."payment_total", 0) AS "order_payment"
    FROM "orders" "o"
    LEFT JOIN "order_payment_totals" "opt"
        ON "o"."order_id" = "opt"."order_id"
    INNER JOIN "customers" "c"
        ON "o"."customer_id" = "c"."customer_id"
),

-- CTE: aggregate per unique customer
"customer_aggregated" AS (
    SELECT
        "customer_unique_id",
        COUNT("order_id") AS "num_orders",
        SUM("order_payment") AS "total_payment",
        MIN("order_purchase_timestamp") AS "earliest_purchase",
        MAX("order_purchase_timestamp") AS "latest_purchase"
    FROM "customer_orders"
    GROUP BY "customer_unique_id"
)

-- Final query: compute averages and lifespan, then top 3
SELECT
    "customer_unique_id",
    "num_orders" AS "number_of_orders",
    ROUND("total_payment" * 1.0 / "num_orders", 4) AS "average_payment_per_order",
    ROUND(
        CASE
            WHEN (JULIANDAY("latest_purchase") - JULIANDAY("earliest_purchase")) / 7.0 < 1.0
            THEN 1.0
            ELSE (JULIANDAY("latest_purchase") - JULIANDAY("earliest_purchase")) / 7.0
        END,
        4
    ) AS "customer_lifespan_weeks"
FROM "customer_aggregated"
ORDER BY "average_payment_per_order" DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 3;
```

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute career totals for each player (games, runs, hits, home runs)
WITH player_totals AS (
    SELECT
        p."player_id",
        p."name_given",
        SUM(b."g") AS "total_g",
        SUM(b."r") AS "total_r",
        SUM(b."h") AS "total_h",

    FROM "player" p
    JOIN "batting" b ON p."player_id" = b."player_id"
    GROUP BY p."player_id", p."name_given"
),
-- Step 2: Find the maximum value for each statistic across all players
max_values AS (
    SELECT
        MAX("total_g") AS "max_g",
        MAX("total_r") AS "max_r",
        MAX("total_h") AS "max_h",
        MAX("total_hr") AS "max_hr"
    FROM "player_totals"
)
-- Step 3: For each statistic, select players whose total equals the maximum
SELECT
    "name_given",
    "total_g" AS "score",
    'games_played' AS "metric"
FROM "player_totals", "max_values"
WHERE "total_g" = "max_g"
UNION ALL
SELECT

    "total_r" AS "score",
    'runs' AS "metric"
FROM "player_totals", "max_values"
WHERE "total_r" = "max_r"

SELECT

SELECT

    "total_hr" AS "score",
    'home_runs' AS "metric"
FROM "player_totals", "max_values"
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
N/A
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- 找出Abakan对应的机场代码
WITH abakan_code AS (
    SELECT "airport_code"
    FROM "airports_data"
    WHERE json_extract("city", '$.en') = 'Abakan'
    LIMIT 1
),
-- 筛选出出发或到达为Abakan的所有航班
relevant_flights AS (
    SELECT f."departure_airport", f."arrival_airport"
    FROM "flights" f
    WHERE f."departure_airport" IN (SELECT "airport_code" FROM abakan_code)
       OR f."arrival_airport" IN (SELECT "airport_code" FROM abakan_code)
),
-- 提取出发和到达机场的经纬度（坐标格式为 (经度,纬度) ）
coords AS (
    SELECT 
        rf."departure_airport",
        rf."arrival_airport",
        -- 出发机场经度
        CAST(SUBSTR(REPLACE(REPLACE(dep."coordinates", '(', ''), ')', ''), 
                    1, INSTR(REPLACE(REPLACE(dep."coordinates", '(', ''), ')', ''), ',') - 1) AS REAL) AS dep_lon,
        -- 出发机场纬度
        CAST(SUBSTR(REPLACE(REPLACE(dep."coordinates", '(', ''), ')', ''), 
                    INSTR(REPLACE(REPLACE(dep."coordinates", '(', ''), ')', ''), ',') + 1) AS REAL) AS dep_lat,
        -- 到达机场经度
        CAST(SUBSTR(REPLACE(REPLACE(arr."coordinates", '(', ''), ')', ''), 
                    1, INSTR(REPLACE(REPLACE(arr."coordinates", '(', ''), ')', ''), ',') - 1) AS REAL) AS arr_lon,
        -- 到达机场纬度
        CAST(SUBSTR(REPLACE(REPLACE(arr."coordinates", '(', ''), ')', ''), 
                    INSTR(REPLACE(REPLACE(arr."coordinates", '(', ''), ')', ''), ',') + 1) AS REAL) AS arr_lat
    FROM relevant_flights rf
    JOIN airports_data dep ON rf."departure_airport" = dep."airport_code"
    JOIN airports_data arr ON rf."arrival_airport" = arr."airport_code"
)
-- 使用Haversine公式计算每条航线的距离，并取最大值
SELECT ROUND(MAX(
    2 * 6371 * ASIN(SQRT(
        SIN((arr_lat * 3.141592653589793 / 180 - dep_lat * 3.141592653589793 / 180) / 2) *
        SIN((arr_lat * 3.141592653589793 / 180 - dep_lat * 3.141592653589793 / 180) / 2) +
        COS(dep_lat * 3.141592653589793 / 180) * COS(arr_lat * 3.141592653589793 / 180) *
        SIN((arr_lon * 3.141592653589793 / 180 - dep_lon * 3.141592653589793 / 180) / 2) *
        SIN((arr_lon * 3.141592653589793 / 180 - dep_lon * 3.141592653589793 / 180) / 2)
    ))
), 4) AS longest_route_distance_km
FROM coords;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute yearly counts of collision causes (pcf_violation_category)
WITH yearly_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        strftime('%Y', "collision_date") AS "year",
        "pcf_violation_category" AS "cause",
        COUNT(*) AS "cnt"
    FROM "collisions"
    WHERE "pcf_violation_category" IS NOT NULL 
      AND "pcf_violation_category" != 'None'
    GROUP BY "year", "cause"
),
-- Step 2: Rank causes within each year by frequency (descending)
ranked_causes AS (
    SELECT 
        "year",
        "cause",
        "cnt",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY "year" 
            ORDER BY "cnt" DESC, "cause"
        ) AS "rn"
    FROM yearly_counts
),
-- Step 3: Keep only the top two causes per year
top2_causes AS (
    SELECT "year", "cause"
    FROM ranked_causes
    WHERE "rn" <= 2
),
-- Step 4: Aggregate the two causes into a comma-separated set per year
year_sets AS (
    SELECT 
        "year",
        GROUP_CONCAT("cause", ', ' ORDER BY "cause") AS "cause_set"
    FROM top2_causes
    GROUP BY "year"
)
-- Step 5: Find years where the set of top two causes is unique (appears only once)
SELECT "year"
FROM year_sets
WHERE "cause_set" NOT IN (
    SELECT "cause_set"
    FROM year_sets
    GROUP BY "cause_set"
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
);
```
</details>

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute total collisions per year for 2011 and 2021
WITH totals AS (
    SELECT 
        strftime('%Y', "collision_date") AS "year",
        COUNT(*) AS "total"
    FROM "collisions"
    WHERE strftime('%Y', "collision_date") IN ('2011', '2021')
    GROUP BY "year"
),

-- Step 2: Count collisions per violation category per year
cat_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        strftime('%Y', "collision_date") AS "year",
        "pcf_violation_category" AS "category",
        COUNT(*) AS "cnt"
    FROM "collisions"
    WHERE strftime('%Y', "collision_date") IN ('2011', '2021')
      AND "pcf_violation_category" IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY "year", "category"
),

-- Step 3: Find the most common category in 2021 (highest count)
top_cat AS (
    SELECT "category", "cnt" AS "cnt2021"
    FROM cat_counts
    WHERE "year" = '2021'
    ORDER BY "cnt" DESC
    LIMIT 1
)

-- Step 4: Compute shares for that category in both years and the decrease
SELECT 
    ROUND(
        ( (SELECT "cnt" FROM cat_counts WHERE "year" = '2011' AND "category" = (SELECT "category" FROM top_cat)) * 100.0 
          / (SELECT "total" FROM totals WHERE "year" = '2011') )
        -
        ( (SELECT "cnt" FROM cat_counts WHERE "year" = '2021' AND "category" = (SELECT "category" FROM top_cat)) * 100.0 
          / (SELECT "total" FROM totals WHERE "year" = '2021') )
    , 4) AS "percentage_points_decrease"
FROM top_cat;
```
</details>

### 178. local026 (DB: `IPL`)
**Question**: Please help me identify the top 3 bowlers who, in the overs where the maximum runs were conceded in each match, gave up the highest number of runs in a single over across all matches. For each of these bowlers, provide the match in which they conceded these maximum runs. Only consider overs that had the most runs conceded within their respective matches, and among these, determine which bowlers conceded the most runs in a single over overall.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

| player_name    |   match_id |   runs_conceded_in_over |
|:---------------|-----------:|------------------------:|
| P Parameswaran |     501252 |                      37 |
| RS Bopara      |     419144 |                      33 |
| P Awana        |     734052 |                      33 |

</details>

<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
N/A
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute total runs conceded per over (including extras) for each bowler
WITH runs_per_over AS (
    SELECT
        b."match_id",
        b."innings_no",
        b."over_id",
        b."bowler",
        COALESCE(SUM(bs."runs_scored"), 0) + COALESCE(SUM(er."extra_runs"), 0) AS total_runs
    FROM "ball_by_ball" b
    LEFT JOIN "batsman_scored" bs
        ON b."match_id" = bs."match_id"
        AND b."innings_no" = bs."innings_no"
        AND b."over_id" = bs."over_id"
        AND b."ball_id" = bs."ball_id"
    LEFT JOIN "extra_runs" er
        ON b."match_id" = er."match_id"
        AND b."innings_no" = er."innings_no"
        AND b."over_id" = er."over_id"
        AND b."ball_id" = er."ball_id"
    GROUP BY b."match_id", b."innings_no", b."over_id", b."bowler"
),

-- Step 2: Identify the maximum runs conceded in any over of each match
max_runs_per_match AS (
    SELECT
        "match_id",
        MAX("total_runs") AS match_max_runs
    FROM runs_per_over
    GROUP BY "match_id"
),

-- Step 3: Keep only the overs that are the highest-run overs in their respective matches
selected_overs AS (
    SELECT
        rpo."match_id",
        rpo."innings_no",
        rpo."over_id",
        rpo."bowler",
        rpo."total_runs"
    FROM runs_per_over rpo
    INNER JOIN max_runs_per_match mrm
        ON rpo."match_id" = mrm."match_id"
        AND rpo."total_runs" = mrm."match_max_runs"
),

-- Step 4: For each bowler, find the maximum runs among the selected overs, and the match where it occurred
bowler_best_over AS (
    SELECT
        "bowler",
        "total_runs" AS best_runs,
        "match_id",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY "bowler"
            ORDER BY "total_runs" DESC, "match_id"
        ) AS rn
    FROM selected_overs
),

-- Step 5: Rank bowlers by their best runs, take top 3
top_bowlers AS (
    SELECT
        "bowler",
        "best_runs",
        "match_id"
    FROM bowler_best_over
    WHERE rn = 1
    ORDER BY "best_runs" DESC
    LIMIT 3
)

-- Final: Join with player to get player name
SELECT
    p."player_name",
    tb."match_id",
    tb."best_runs" AS runs_conceded_in_over
FROM top_bowlers tb
JOIN "player" p ON tb."bowler" = p."player_id";
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: For each delivery, compute total runs conceded by the bowler
-- (including runs off the bat and extras that are charged to the bowler: wides and noballs)
WITH delivery_runs AS (
    SELECT
        b."match_id",
        b."innings_no",
        b."over_id",
        b."ball_id",
        b."bowler",
        COALESCE(SUM(bs."runs_scored"), 0) AS bat_runs,
        COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN e."extra_type" IN ('wides','noballs') THEN e."extra_runs" ELSE 0 END), 0) AS extra_runs_charged
    FROM "ball_by_ball" b
    LEFT JOIN "batsman_scored" bs
        ON b."match_id" = bs."match_id"
        AND b."innings_no" = bs."innings_no"
        AND b."over_id" = bs."over_id"
        AND b."ball_id" = bs."ball_id"
    LEFT JOIN "extra_runs" e
        ON b."match_id" = e."match_id"
        AND b."innings_no" = e."innings_no"
        AND b."over_id" = e."over_id"
        AND b."ball_id" = e."ball_id"
    GROUP BY
        b."match_id",
        b."innings_no",
        b."over_id",
        b."ball_id",
        b."bowler"
),

-- Step 2: For each wicket, identify the bowler who took it
wickets AS (
    SELECT
        w."match_id",
        w."innings_no",
        w."over_id",
        w."ball_id",
        b."bowler"
    FROM "wicket_taken" w
    JOIN "ball_by_ball" b
        ON w."match_id" = b."match_id"
        AND w."innings_no" = b."innings_no"
        AND w."over_id" = b."over_id"
        AND w."ball_id" = b."ball_id"
),

-- Step 3: Aggregate per bowler: total runs conceded and total wickets
bowler_stats AS (
    SELECT
        dr."bowler",
        SUM(dr."bat_runs" + dr."extra_runs_charged") AS runs_conceded,
        COUNT(w."bowler") AS wickets_taken
    FROM delivery_runs dr
    LEFT JOIN wickets w
        ON dr."match_id" = w."match_id"
        AND dr."innings_no" = w."innings_no"
        AND dr."over_id" = w."over_id"
        AND dr."ball_id" = w."ball_id"
        AND dr."bowler" = w."bowler"
    GROUP BY dr."bowler"
    HAVING wickets_taken > 0  -- exclude bowlers with zero wickets (infinite average)
)

-- Step 4: Compute bowling average and get the bowler with the lowest value
SELECT
    p."player_id",
    p."player_name",
    ROUND(bs.runs_conceded * 1.0 / bs.wickets_taken, 4) AS bowling_average
FROM bowler_stats bs
JOIN "player" p ON bs."bowler" = p."player_id"
ORDER BY bowling_average ASC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute runs per striker per innings (match + innings)
WITH "innings_totals" AS (
    SELECT
        "b"."striker",
        "b"."match_id",
        "b"."innings_no",
        SUM("s"."runs_scored") AS "innings_total"
    FROM "ball_by_ball" AS "b"
    INNER JOIN "batsman_scored" AS "s"
        ON "b"."match_id" = "s"."match_id"
        AND "b"."innings_no" = "s"."innings_no"
        AND "b"."over_id" = "s"."over_id"
        AND "b"."ball_id" = "s"."ball_id"
    GROUP BY
        "b"."striker",
        "b"."match_id",
        "b"."innings_no"
),
-- Step 2: Identify strikers who have at least one innings with total > 50
"qualifying_strikers" AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "striker"
    FROM "innings_totals"
    WHERE "innings_total" > 50
),
-- Step 3: For those strikers, sum their career runs (all innings)
"striker_total_runs" AS (
    SELECT
        "it"."striker",
        SUM("it"."innings_total") AS "total_runs"
    FROM "innings_totals" AS "it"
    WHERE "it"."striker" IN (SELECT "striker" FROM "qualifying_strikers")
    GROUP BY "it"."striker"
)
-- Step 4: Average of the career totals
SELECT
    ROUND(AVG("total_runs"), 4) AS "avg_total_runs"
FROM "striker_total_runs";
```

```sql
-- CTE to calculate total runs per player per match
WITH player_runs AS (
    SELECT 
        bbb.match_id,
        bbb.striker AS player_id,
        SUM(bs.runs_scored) AS total_runs
    FROM 
        "ball_by_ball" bbb
    INNER JOIN

        AND bbb.innings_no = bs.innings_no

),

        pm.match_id,
        pm.player_id,
        pm.team_id
    FROM

)
-- Final selection: player names matching criteria
SELECT DISTINCT
    p.player_name
FROM 
    player_runs pr
INNER JOIN 
    player_team pt 
    ON pr.match_id = pt.match_id AND pr.player_id = pt.player_id
INNER JOIN 
    "player" p 
    ON pr.player_id = p.player_id
INNER JOIN 
    "match" m 
    ON pr.match_id = m.match_id
WHERE 
    pr.total_runs >= 100
    AND pt.team_id != m.match_winner
ORDER BY 
    p.player_name;
```

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Filter season 5 matches
season5_matches AS (
    SELECT match_id
    FROM "match"
    WHERE season_id = 5
),

-- Step 2: Get all runs scored by each player in season 5
player_runs AS (
    SELECT 
        b.striker AS player_id,
        b.match_id,
        SUM(bs.runs_scored) AS total_runs_in_match
    FROM ball_by_ball b
    JOIN batsman_scored bs 
        ON b.match_id = bs.match_id 
        AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no 
        AND b.over_id = bs.over_id 
        AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
    WHERE b.match_id IN (SELECT match_id FROM season5_matches)
    GROUP BY b.striker, b.match_id
),

-- Step 3: Compute per-player aggregates
player_season_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        pr.player_id,
        COUNT(pr.match_id) AS matches_played,
        SUM(pr.total_runs_in_match) AS total_runs,
        -- Count dismissals
        (SELECT COUNT(*) 
         FROM wicket_taken wt
         WHERE wt.player_out = pr.player_id
           AND wt.match_id IN (SELECT match_id FROM season5_matches)
        ) AS total_dismissals
    FROM player_runs pr
    GROUP BY pr.player_id
),

-- Step 4: Calculate averages
player_averages AS (
    SELECT 
        pss.player_id,
        p.player_name,
        ROUND(pss.total_runs * 1.0 / pss.matches_played, 4) AS avg_runs_per_match,
        ROUND(pss.total_runs * 1.0 / CASE WHEN pss.total_dismissals = 0 THEN 1 ELSE pss.total_dismissals END, 4) AS batting_average
    FROM player_season_stats pss
    JOIN player p ON pss.player_id = p.player_id
    WHERE pss.matches_played > 0
)

-- Step 5: Select top 5 by avg_runs_per_match
SELECT 
    player_name,
    avg_runs_per_match,
    batting_average
FROM player_averages
ORDER BY avg_runs_per_match DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Compute total runs (batsman scored + extra runs) per ball
per_ball AS (
    SELECT 
        b."match_id",
        b."innings_no",
        b."over_id",
        b."ball_id",
        b."bowler",
        COALESCE(bs."runs_scored", 0) AS runs_scored,
        COALESCE(er.total_extra, 0) AS extra
    FROM "ball_by_ball" b
    LEFT JOIN "batsman_scored" bs 
        ON b."match_id" = bs."match_id" 
        AND b."innings_no" = bs."innings_no" 
        AND b."over_id" = bs."over_id" 
        AND b."ball_id" = bs."ball_id"
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT 
            "match_id",
            "innings_no",
            "over_id",
            "ball_id",
            SUM("extra_runs") AS total_extra
        FROM "extra_runs"
        GROUP BY "match_id", "innings_no", "over_id", "ball_id"
    ) er 
        ON b."match_id" = er."match_id" 
        AND b."innings_no" = er."innings_no" 
        AND b."over_id" = er."over_id" 
        AND b."ball_id" = er."ball_id"
),
-- Step 2: Aggregate runs per over (match, innings, over)
per_over AS (
    SELECT 
        "match_id",
        "innings_no",
        "over_id",
        SUM(runs_scored + extra) AS total_runs
    FROM per_ball
    GROUP BY "match_id", "innings_no", "over_id"
),
-- Step 3: Rank overs per match by total runs descending, pick the single highest
ranked_over AS (
    SELECT 
        "match_id",
        "innings_no",
        "over_id",
        total_runs,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY "match_id" 
            ORDER BY total_runs DESC, "innings_no", "over_id"
        ) AS rn
    FROM per_over
),
-- Step 4: Keep only the top over per match
top_over AS (
    SELECT 
        "match_id",
        "innings_no",
        "over_id",
        total_runs
    FROM ranked_over
    WHERE rn = 1
),
-- Step 5: Retrieve the bowler for that over (any ball from the over)
bowler_for_over AS (
    SELECT 
        t."match_id",
        t."innings_no",
        t."over_id",
        t.total_runs,
        MIN(pb."bowler") AS bowler_id
    FROM top_over t
    JOIN per_ball pb 
        ON t."match_id" = pb."match_id" 
        AND t."innings_no" = pb."innings_no" 
        AND t."over_id" = pb."over_id"
    GROUP BY t."match_id", t."innings_no", t."over_id", t.total_runs
)
-- Step 6: Calculate the average of the highest over totals across all matches
SELECT 
    ROUND(AVG(total_runs), 4) AS avg_highest_over_runs
FROM bowler_for_over;
```
</details>

### 185. local031 (DB: `Brazilian_E_Commerce`)
**Question**: What is the highest monthly delivered orders volume in the year with the lowest annual delivered orders volume among 2016, 2017, and 2018?

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|   HIGHEST_MONTHLY_VOLUME |
|-------------------------:|
|                      205 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|-----------------------------------:|
|                                205 |

<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql

```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Compute annual delivered volumes for 2016, 2017, 2018
annual_volumes AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(strftime('%Y', "order_delivered_customer_date") AS INTEGER) AS year,
        COUNT(*) AS annual_orders
    FROM "olist_orders"
    WHERE 
        "order_status" = 'delivered'
        AND "order_delivered_customer_date" IS NOT NULL
        AND CAST(strftime('%Y', "order_delivered_customer_date") AS INTEGER) IN (2016, 2017, 2018)
    GROUP BY year
),
-- Step 2: Find the year with smallest annual delivered orders
min_year AS (
    SELECT year
    FROM annual_volumes
    ORDER BY annual_orders ASC
    LIMIT 1
),
-- Step 3: For that year, compute monthly delivered volumes
monthly_volumes AS (
    SELECT
        strftime('%Y-%m', "order_delivered_customer_date") AS month,
        COUNT(*) AS monthly_orders
    FROM "olist_orders"
    WHERE 
        "order_status" = 'delivered'
        AND "order_delivered_customer_date" IS NOT NULL
        AND CAST(strftime('%Y', "order_delivered_customer_date") AS INTEGER) = (SELECT year FROM min_year)
    GROUP BY month
)
-- Step 4: Get the highest monthly volume
SELECT MAX(monthly_orders) AS highest_monthly_delivered_orders
FROM monthly_volumes;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH 
-- Get all delivered orders with customer unique id, city, state
delivered_orders AS (
    SELECT 
        c."customer_unique_id",
        c."customer_city",
        c."customer_state",
        o."order_id"
    FROM "olist_orders" o
    JOIN "olist_customers" c ON o."customer_id" = c."customer_id"
    WHERE o."order_status" = 'delivered'
),
-- Count delivered orders per customer
customer_order_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        "customer_unique_id",
        "customer_city",
        "customer_state",
        COUNT("order_id") AS delivered_order_count
    FROM delivered_orders
    GROUP BY "customer_unique_id", "customer_city", "customer_state"
),
-- Get top 3 customers by order count
top3_customers AS (
    SELECT 
        "customer_unique_id",
        "customer_city",
        "customer_state",
        delivered_order_count
    FROM customer_order_counts
    ORDER BY delivered_order_count DESC NULLS LAST
    LIMIT 3
)
-- Final: average payment value for top 3 customers
SELECT 
    t."customer_unique_id",
    ROUND(AVG(p."payment_value"), 4) AS average_payment_value,
    t."customer_city",
    t."customer_state"
FROM top3_customers t
JOIN "olist_customers" c ON t."customer_unique_id" = c."customer_unique_id"
JOIN "olist_orders" o ON c."customer_id" = o."customer_id" AND o."order_status" = 'delivered'
JOIN "olist_order_payments" p ON o."order_id" = p."order_id"
GROUP BY t."customer_unique_id", t."customer_city", t."customer_state", t.delivered_order_count
ORDER BY t.delivered_order_count DESC;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute total payment per order
WITH "order_payment" AS (
    SELECT 
        "order_id",
        SUM("payment_value") AS "total_payment"
    FROM "olist_order_payments"
    GROUP BY "order_id"
),
-- Step 2: Filter delivered orders and attach payment
"delivered_orders" AS (
    SELECT 
        o."order_id",
        o."customer_id",
        p."total_payment"
    FROM "olist_orders" o
    INNER JOIN "order_payment" p ON o."order_id" = p."order_id"
    WHERE o."order_status" = 'delivered'
),
-- Step 3: Join customer city
"customer_city" AS (
    SELECT 
        d."order_id",
        d."total_payment",
        c."customer_city"
    FROM "delivered_orders" d
    INNER JOIN "olist_customers" c ON d."customer_id" = c."customer_id"
),
-- Step 4: Aggregate per city
"city_aggregates" AS (
    SELECT 
        "customer_city" AS "city",
        SUM("total_payment") AS "city_total_payment",
        COUNT(*) AS "city_order_count"
    FROM "customer_city"
    GROUP BY "customer_city"
),
-- Step 5: Select the 5 cities with lowest total payment
"top5_cities" AS (
    SELECT 
        "city",
        "city_total_payment",
        "city_order_count"
    FROM "city_aggregates"
    ORDER BY "city_total_payment" ASC NULLS LAST
    LIMIT 5
)
-- Step 6: Compute averages
SELECT 
    ROUND(AVG("city_total_payment"), 4) AS "avg_total_payment",
    ROUND(AVG("city_order_count"), 4) AS "avg_order_count"
FROM "top5_cities";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- CTE 1: Distinct customer unique IDs per seller (delivered only)
customer_count AS (
    SELECT
        oi."seller_id",
        COUNT(DISTINCT c."customer_unique_id") AS value
    FROM "olist_order_items" oi
    JOIN "olist_orders" o ON oi."order_id" = o."order_id"
    JOIN "olist_customers" c ON o."customer_id" = c."customer_id"
    WHERE o."order_status" = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY oi."seller_id"
),

-- CTE 2: Profit (price - freight_value) per seller (delivered only)
profit_sum AS (
    SELECT
        oi."seller_id",
        ROUND(SUM(oi."price" - oi."freight_value"), 4) AS value
    FROM "olist_order_items" oi
    JOIN "olist_orders" o ON oi."order_id" = o."order_id"
    WHERE o."order_status" = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY oi."seller_id"
),

-- CTE 3: Distinct order count per seller (delivered only)
order_count AS (
    SELECT
        oi."seller_id",
        COUNT(DISTINCT oi."order_id") AS value
    FROM "olist_order_items" oi
    JOIN "olist_orders" o ON oi."order_id" = o."order_id"
    WHERE o."order_status" = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY oi."seller_id"
),

-- CTE 4: Count of 5-star ratings per seller (delivered only)
-- Corrected to count distinct reviews (each order has one review)
five_star_count AS (
    SELECT
        oi."seller_id",
        COUNT(DISTINCT r."review_id") AS value
    FROM "olist_order_items" oi
    JOIN "olist_orders" o ON oi."order_id" = o."order_id"
    JOIN "olist_order_reviews" r ON o."order_id" = r."order_id"
    WHERE o."order_status" = 'delivered'
      AND r."review_score" = 5
    GROUP BY oi."seller_id"
)

-- Final UNION ALL with subqueries to allow ORDER BY + LIMIT per category
SELECT *
FROM (
    SELECT
        'Highest distinct customer IDs' AS achievement,
        "seller_id",
        value
    FROM customer_count
    ORDER BY value DESC NULLS LAST
    LIMIT 1
) AS sub1

UNION ALL

SELECT *
FROM (
    SELECT
        'Highest profit (price - freight)' AS achievement,
        "seller_id",
        value
    FROM profit_sum
    ORDER BY value DESC NULLS LAST
    LIMIT 1
) AS sub2

UNION ALL

SELECT *
FROM (
    SELECT
        'Highest number of distinct orders' AS achievement,
        "seller_id",
        value
    FROM order_count
    ORDER BY value DESC NULLS LAST
    LIMIT 1
) AS sub3

UNION ALL

SELECT *
FROM (
    SELECT
        'Most 5-star ratings' AS achievement,
        "seller_id",
        value
    FROM five_star_count
    ORDER BY value DESC NULLS LAST
    LIMIT 1
) AS sub4;
```
</details>

<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>


<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Compute the average of the total number of payments for the most preferred payment method per product category.
-- The preferred method is the one with the highest count of payment rows in that category.

WITH
-- Step 1: Get distinct payment rows (order_id, payment_sequential) per product category
-- to avoid double-counting when an order has multiple items in the same category.
"payment_category" AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        "op"."order_id",
        "op"."payment_sequential",
        "op"."payment_type",
        "p"."product_category_name"
    FROM "olist_order_payments" AS "op"
    INNER JOIN "olist_order_items" AS "oi"
        ON "op"."order_id" = "oi"."order_id"
    INNER JOIN "olist_products" AS "p"
        ON "oi"."product_id" = "p"."product_id"
),

-- Step 2: Count payment rows for each category and each payment method
"category_method_counts" AS (
    SELECT
        "product_category_name",
        "payment_type",
        COUNT(*) AS "cnt"
    FROM "payment_category"
    GROUP BY "product_category_name", "payment_type"
),

-- Step 3: Rank methods within each category by count descending (use payment_type as tie-breaker)
"ranked" AS (
    SELECT
        "product_category_name",
        "payment_type",
        "cnt",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY "product_category_name"
            ORDER BY "cnt" DESC, "payment_type"
        ) AS "rn"
    FROM "category_method_counts"
),

-- Step 4: Keep only the top-ranked method per category
"top_method" AS (
    SELECT
        "product_category_name",
        "payment_type",
        "cnt"
    FROM "ranked"
    WHERE "rn" = 1
)

-- Step 5: Average the total number of payments (cnt) across all categories
SELECT
    ROUND(AVG("cnt"), 4) AS "avg_top_method_total"
FROM "top_method";
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Distinct (order_id, product_category_name) per order
WITH OrderCategories AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        oi."order_id",
        p."product_category_name"
    FROM "olist_order_items" oi
    JOIN "olist_products" p ON oi."product_id" = p."product_id"
    WHERE p."product_category_name" IS NOT NULL   -- exclude unknown categories
),

-- Step 2: Attach each payment to every category in its order
CategoryPayments AS (
    SELECT
        oc."product_category_name",
        op."payment_type"
    FROM OrderCategories oc
    JOIN "olist_order_payments" op ON oc."order_id" = op."order_id"
),

-- Step 3: Count payments per category and payment type
CategoryPaymentCounts AS (
    SELECT
        "product_category_name",
        "payment_type",
        COUNT(*) AS "payment_count"
    FROM CategoryPayments
    GROUP BY "product_category_name", "payment_type"
),

-- Step 4: For each category, find the most common payment type (highest count)
RankedCategories AS (
    SELECT
        "product_category_name",
        "payment_type",
        "payment_count",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY "product_category_name"
            ORDER BY "payment_count" DESC, "payment_type" ASC   -- break ties alphabetically
        ) AS "rn"
    FROM CategoryPaymentCounts
)

-- Step 5: Select top 3 categories by the count of their most common payment type
SELECT
    "product_category_name",
    "payment_count" AS "number_of_payments_using_most_common_type"
FROM RankedCategories
WHERE "rn" = 1
ORDER BY "payment_count" DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 3;
```
</details>

```sql
            "geolocation_lng"
        ) AS lat1,
        LAG("geolocation_lng") OVER (ORDER BY 
            "geolocation_state",
            "geolocation_city",
            "geolocation_zip_code_prefix",
            "geolocation_lat",
            "geolocation_lng"
        ) AS lng1
    FROM ordered_geo
)
SELECT 
    city1 AS city_prev,
    state1 AS state_prev,
    city2 AS city_next,
    state2 AS state_next,
    ROUND(
        6371 * ACOS(
            COS(RADIANS(lat1)) * COS(RADIANS(lat2)) * 
            COS(RADIANS(lng2) - RADIANS(lng1)) + 
            SIN(RADIANS(lat1)) * SIN(RADIANS(lat2))
        ),
        4
    ) AS distance_km
FROM with_prev
WHERE city1 IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY distance_km DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH 
-- Filter films that meet all criteria
qualified_films AS (
    SELECT 
        f.film_id,
        f.title,
        f.rating,
        f.length,
        f.release_year
    FROM "film" f
    INNER JOIN "language" l ON f.language_id = l.language_id
    INNER JOIN "film_category" fc ON f.film_id = fc.film_id
    INNER JOIN "category" c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
    WHERE 
        LOWER(l.name) = 'english'          -- English language
        AND LOWER(c.name) = 'children'     -- Children category
        AND f.rating IN ('G', 'PG')        -- Ratings G or PG
        AND f.length <= 120                -- Running time ≤ 120 minutes
        AND f.release_year BETWEEN '2000' AND '2010'  -- Released between 2000 and 2010
),
-- Count appearances per actor in qualified films
actor_film_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        a.actor_id,
        a.first_name,
        a.last_name,
        COUNT(qf.film_id) AS film_count
    FROM "actor" a
    INNER JOIN "film_actor" fa ON a.actor_id = fa.actor_id
    INNER JOIN qualified_films qf ON fa.film_id = qf.film_id
    GROUP BY a.actor_id, a.first_name, a.last_name
)
-- Return the actor with the highest count (most frequent)
SELECT 
    first_name || ' ' || last_name AS actor_full_name,
    film_count
FROM actor_film_counts
ORDER BY film_count DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify cities that start with 'A' or contain a hyphen
WITH filtered_cities AS (
    SELECT "city_id"
    FROM "city"
    WHERE LOWER("city") LIKE 'a%'
       OR "city" LIKE '%-%'
),

-- Step 2: Compute rental hours for each rental in those cities, linking film_id
rental_hours_per_film AS (
    SELECT
        r."rental_id",
        i."film_id",
        (julianday(r."return_date") - julianday(r."rental_date")) * 24 AS "hours"
    FROM "rental" r
    JOIN "inventory" i ON r."inventory_id" = i."inventory_id"
    JOIN "customer" c ON r."customer_id" = c."customer_id"
    JOIN "address" a ON c."address_id" = a."address_id"
    JOIN filtered_cities fc ON a."city_id" = fc."city_id"
    WHERE r."return_date" IS NOT NULL
)

-- Step 3: Aggregate rental hours by category and pick the highest
SELECT
    ca."category_id",
    ca."name" AS "category_name",
    ROUND(SUM(rh."hours"), 4) AS "total_rental_hours"
FROM rental_hours_per_film rh
JOIN "film_category" fc ON rh."film_id" = fc."film_id"
JOIN "category" ca ON fc."category_id" = ca."category_id"
GROUP BY ca."category_id", ca."name"
ORDER BY "total_rental_hours" DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

### 198. local055 (DB: `chinook`)
**Question**: Identify the artist with the highest overall sales of albums (tie broken by alphabetical order) and the artist with the lowest overall sales of albums (tie broken by alphabetical order), then calculate the amount each customer spent specifically on those two artists’ albums. Next, compute the average spending for the customers who purchased from the top-selling artist and the average spending for the customers who purchased from the lowest-selling artist, and finally return the absolute difference between these two averages.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|   average_spending_difference |
|------------------------------:|
|                       5.13333 |

**OR**

|   AbsoluteAverageDifference |
|----------------------------:|
|                     4.14333 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|   avg_difference |
|-----------------:|
|           4.1433 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
N/A
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute total sales per artist (sum of invoice line items for tracks in their albums)
WITH artist_sales AS (
    SELECT 
        a."ArtistId",
        ar."Name",
        SUM(ii."UnitPrice" * ii."Quantity") AS total_sales
    FROM "invoice_items" ii
    JOIN "tracks" t ON ii."TrackId" = t."TrackId"
    JOIN "albums" a ON t."AlbumId" = a."AlbumId"
    JOIN "artists" ar ON a."ArtistId" = ar."ArtistId"
    GROUP BY a."ArtistId", ar."Name"
),

-- Step 2: Identify top-selling artist (highest total sales, tie broken by artist name alphabetically)
top_artist AS (
    SELECT "ArtistId", "Name", total_sales
    FROM artist_sales
    ORDER BY total_sales DESC, "Name" ASC
    LIMIT 1
),

-- Step 3: Identify lowest-selling artist (lowest total sales, tie broken by artist name alphabetically)
bottom_artist AS (
    SELECT "ArtistId", "Name", total_sales
    FROM artist_sales
    ORDER BY total_sales ASC, "Name" ASC
    LIMIT 1
),

-- Step 4: For each customer, compute their spending on the top-selling artist’s albums
customer_spending_top AS (
    SELECT 
        c."CustomerId",
        SUM(ii."UnitPrice" * ii."Quantity") AS artist_spending
    FROM "customers" c
    JOIN "invoices" i ON c."CustomerId" = i."CustomerId"
    JOIN "invoice_items" ii ON i."InvoiceId" = ii."InvoiceId"
    JOIN "tracks" t ON ii."TrackId" = t."TrackId"
    JOIN "albums" a ON t."AlbumId" = a."AlbumId"
    WHERE a."ArtistId" = (SELECT "ArtistId" FROM top_artist)
    GROUP BY c."CustomerId"
),

-- Step 5: For each customer, compute their spending on the lowest-selling artist’s albums
customer_spending_bottom AS (
    SELECT 
        c."CustomerId",
        SUM(ii."UnitPrice" * ii."Quantity") AS artist_spending
    FROM "customers" c
    JOIN "invoices" i ON c."CustomerId" = i."CustomerId"
    JOIN "invoice_items" ii ON i."InvoiceId" = ii."InvoiceId"
    JOIN "tracks" t ON ii."TrackId" = t."TrackId"
    JOIN "albums" a ON t."AlbumId" = a."AlbumId"
    WHERE a."ArtistId" = (SELECT "ArtistId" FROM bottom_artist)
    GROUP BY c."CustomerId"
),

-- Step 6: Compute average spending for customers who purchased from each artist
avg_top AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(AVG(artist_spending), 0) AS avg_spending
    FROM customer_spending_top
),

avg_bottom AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(AVG(artist_spending), 0) AS avg_spending
    FROM customer_spending_bottom
)

-- Final: Absolute difference between the two averages, rounded to 4 decimal places
SELECT ROUND(ABS(avg_top.avg_spending - avg_bottom.avg_spending), 4) AS avg_difference
FROM avg_top, avg_bottom;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Find countries with more than 4 customers
"customer_counts" AS (
    SELECT 
        "c"."Country",
        COUNT(DISTINCT "c"."CustomerId") AS "customer_count"
    FROM "customers" "c"
    GROUP BY "c"."Country"
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT "c"."CustomerId") > 4
),
-- Step 2: Calculate total sales per country for those qualifying countries
"total_sales_per_country" AS (
    SELECT 
        "c"."Country",
        ROUND(SUM("i"."Total"), 4) AS "total_sales"
    FROM "customers" "c"
    INNER JOIN "invoices" "i" ON "c"."CustomerId" = "i"."CustomerId"
    WHERE "c"."Country" IN (SELECT "Country" FROM "customer_counts")
    GROUP BY "c"."Country"
),
-- Step 3: Compute median using SQLite approach
"ordered_sales" AS (
    SELECT 
        "total_sales",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "total_sales") AS "row_num",
        COUNT(*) OVER () AS "total_count"
    FROM "total_sales_per_country"
)
SELECT 
    ROUND(AVG("total_sales"), 4) AS "median_total_sales"
FROM "ordered_sales"
WHERE 
    "row_num" IN (
        (("total_count" + 1) / 2),
        (("total_count" + 2) / 2)
    );
```
</details>

```sql
WITH

    FROM products_2021

FROM counts_2020 c20
```

```sql
WITH
    -- Step 1: Filter sales for calendar year 2021 and join with product to get division
    sales_2021 AS (
        SELECT
            s."product_code",
            p."division",
            s."sold_quantity"
        FROM "hardware_fact_sales_monthly" s
        JOIN "hardware_dim_product" p ON s."product_code" = p."product_code"
        WHERE strftime('%Y', s."date") = '2021'
    ),
    -- Step 2: Aggregate total quantity sold per product per division in 2021
    product_totals AS (
        SELECT
            "division",
            "product_code",
            SUM("sold_quantity") AS total_qty
        FROM sales_2021
        GROUP BY "division", "product_code"
    ),
    -- Step 3: Rank products within each division by total quantity descending
    ranked_products AS (
        SELECT
            "division",
            "product_code",
            "total_qty",
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                PARTITION BY "division"
                ORDER BY "total_qty" DESC, "product_code" ASC  -- tie-breaker by product_code
            ) AS rn
        FROM product_totals
    ),
    -- Step 4: Select top 3 per division
    top3 AS (
        SELECT
            "division",
            "product_code",
            "total_qty"
        FROM ranked_products
        WHERE rn <= 3
    )
-- Step 5: Compute overall average quantity sold of those top 3 products per division
SELECT
    "division",
    ROUND(AVG("total_qty"), 4) AS avg_quantity_sold_top3
FROM top3
GROUP BY "division"
ORDER BY "division";
```

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify US customers (city level)
WITH us_customers AS (
    SELECT c.cust_id, c.cust_city
    FROM customers c
    JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
    WHERE co.country_name = 'United States of America'
),

-- Step 2: Sales with no promotion (promo_id = 999) in Q4 2019 and Q4 2020, only US customers
sales_us_no_promo AS (
    SELECT s.amount_sold, s.prod_id, u.cust_city, t.calendar_year
    FROM sales s
    JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
    JOIN us_customers u ON s.cust_id = u.cust_id
    WHERE s.promo_id = 999
      AND t.calendar_quarter_number = 4
      AND t.calendar_year IN (2019, 2020)
),

-- Step 3: City-level total sales per quarter
city_sales_agg AS (
    SELECT cust_city, calendar_year, SUM(amount_sold) AS city_sales
    FROM sales_us_no_promo
    GROUP BY cust_city, calendar_year
),

-- Step 4: Pivot to get 2019 and 2020 sales per city
city_sales_pivot AS (
    SELECT cust_city,
           COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN calendar_year = 2019 THEN city_sales END), 0) AS sales_2019,
           COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN calendar_year = 2020 THEN city_sales END), 0) AS sales_2020
    FROM city_sales_agg
    GROUP BY cust_city
),

-- Step 5: Filter cities where sales grew by at least 20%
qualified_cities AS (
    SELECT cust_city
    FROM city_sales_pivot
    WHERE sales_2019 > 0
      AND (sales_2020 - sales_2019) / sales_2019 >= 0.20
),

-- Step 6: Product-level total sales (both quarters) within qualified cities
product_sales_total AS (
    SELECT prod_id, SUM(amount_sold) AS total_sales
    FROM sales_us_no_promo
    WHERE cust_city IN (SELECT cust_city FROM qualified_cities)
    GROUP BY prod_id
),

-- Step 7: Use NTILE(5) to get top 20% products by total sales
ranked_products AS (
    SELECT prod_id, total_sales,
           NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY total_sales DESC) AS bucket
    FROM product_sales_total
),
top_products AS (
    SELECT prod_id FROM ranked_products WHERE bucket = 1
),

-- Step 8: Per‑quarter sales for top products within qualified cities
product_quarter_sales AS (
    SELECT prod_id, calendar_year, SUM(amount_sold) AS prod_sales
    FROM sales_us_no_promo
    WHERE cust_city IN (SELECT cust_city FROM qualified_cities)
      AND prod_id IN (SELECT prod_id FROM top_products)
    GROUP BY prod_id, calendar_year
),

-- Step 9: Total sales per quarter within qualified cities
total_quarter_sales AS (
    SELECT calendar_year, SUM(amount_sold) AS total_sales_q
    FROM sales_us_no_promo
    WHERE cust_city IN (SELECT cust_city FROM qualified_cities)
    GROUP BY calendar_year
),

-- Step 10: Compute share for each product per quarter
product_shares AS (
    SELECT p.prod_id, p.calendar_year,
           p.prod_sales / t.total_sales_q AS share
    FROM product_quarter_sales p
    JOIN total_quarter_sales t ON p.calendar_year = t.calendar_year
),

-- Step 11: Pivot to get share_2019 and share_2020 for each product
shares_pivot AS (
    SELECT prod_id,
           MAX(CASE WHEN calendar_year = 2019 THEN share ELSE 0 END) AS share_2019,
           MAX(CASE WHEN calendar_year = 2020 THEN share ELSE 0 END) AS share_2020
    FROM product_shares
    GROUP BY prod_id
),

-- Step 12: Compute share change
share_diff AS (
    SELECT prod_id, share_2019, share_2020,
           share_2020 - share_2019 AS share_change
    FROM shares_pivot
)

-- Final output: product name, product id, shares, and change, ordered descending by change
SELECT p.prod_name, p.prod_id,
       ROUND(s.share_2019, 4) AS share_2019,
       ROUND(s.share_2020, 4) AS share_2020,
       ROUND(s.share_change, 4) AS share_change
FROM share_diff s
JOIN products p ON s.prod_id = p.prod_id
ORDER BY share_change DESC NULLS LAST;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
/*
  Step-by-step reasoning:

  1. Identify the scope: Only sales in the United States (country_name = 'United States of America')
     with promo_id = 999, in Q4 2019 (calendar_quarter_id = 1772) and Q4 2020 (calendar_quarter_id = 1776).

  2. For each city (cust_city), compute total sales (amount_sold) in each quarter.
     Keep only cities where the increase from Q4 2019 to Q4 2020 is at least 20%.

  3. Within those cities, for each product, compute:
     - total sales in each quarter
     - share of total sales in each quarter (product sales / overall sales in that quarter)
     - percentage-point change = share_2020 - share_2019 (absolute value used for ordering)
     - total sales across both quarters (to determine top 20% ranking)

  4. Determine the top 20% of products by total sales using NTILE(5) (bucket 1 = highest 20%).
     Among them, pick the product with the smallest absolute percentage-point change.

  5. Return the product id and product name of that product.
*/

WITH
  -- Step 1: base sales with necessary joins
  base_sales AS (
    SELECT
      s.prod_id,
      s.amount_sold,
      s.time_id,
      c.cust_city,
      c.cust_city_id,
      t.calendar_quarter_id
    FROM sales s
    JOIN customers c ON s.cust_id = c.cust_id
    JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
    JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
    WHERE
      co.country_name = 'United States of America'
      AND s.promo_id = 999
      AND t.calendar_quarter_id IN (1772, 1776)
  ),

  -- Step 2: city-level sales per quarter and identify qualifying cities
  city_quarter_sales AS (
    SELECT
      cust_city_id,
      cust_city,
      calendar_quarter_id,
      SUM(amount_sold) AS total_sales
    FROM base_sales
    GROUP BY cust_city_id, cust_city, calendar_quarter_id
  ),
  city_growth AS (
    SELECT
      a.cust_city_id,
      a.cust_city,
      a.total_sales AS sales_2019,
      b.total_sales AS sales_2020,
      (b.total_sales - a.total_sales) * 100.0 / a.total_sales AS pct_increase
    FROM city_quarter_sales a
    JOIN city_quarter_sales b
      ON a.cust_city_id = b.cust_city_id
    WHERE
      a.calendar_quarter_id = 1772
      AND b.calendar_quarter_id = 1776
      AND a.total_sales > 0
  ),
  valid_cities AS (
    SELECT cust_city_id
    FROM city_growth
    WHERE pct_increase >= 20.0
  ),

  -- Step 3: product-level sales and shares within valid cities
  product_quarter_sales AS (
    SELECT
      s.prod_id,
      s.calendar_quarter_id,
      SUM(s.amount_sold) AS prod_sales
    FROM base_sales s
    JOIN valid_cities vc ON s.cust_city_id = vc.cust_city_id
    GROUP BY s.prod_id, s.calendar_quarter_id
  ),
  quarter_total_sales AS (
    SELECT
      calendar_quarter_id,
      SUM(prod_sales) AS total_sales
    FROM product_quarter_sales
    GROUP BY calendar_quarter_id
  ),
  product_shares AS (
    SELECT
      p.prod_id,
      MAX(CASE WHEN p.calendar_quarter_id = 1772 THEN p.prod_sales END) AS sales_2019,
      MAX(CASE WHEN p.calendar_quarter_id = 1776 THEN p.prod_sales END) AS sales_2020,
      MAX(CASE WHEN p.calendar_quarter_id = 1772 THEN p.prod_sales END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(MAX(CASE WHEN q.calendar_quarter_id = 1772 THEN q.total_sales END), 0) AS share_2019,
      MAX(CASE WHEN p.calendar_quarter_id = 1776 THEN p.prod_sales END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(MAX(CASE WHEN q.calendar_quarter_id = 1776 THEN q.total_sales END), 0) AS share_2020,
      COALESCE(MAX(CASE WHEN p.calendar_quarter_id = 1772 THEN p.prod_sales END), 0) + COALESCE(MAX(CASE WHEN p.calendar_quarter_id = 1776 THEN p.prod_sales END), 0) AS total_sales_both
    FROM product_quarter_sales p
    CROSS JOIN quarter_total_sales q
    GROUP BY p.prod_id
  ),
  product_share_change AS (
    SELECT
      prod_id,
      share_2019,
      share_2020,
      ROUND(ABS(share_2020 - share_2019), 4) AS abs_ppt_change,
      total_sales_both
    FROM product_shares
    WHERE share_2019 IS NOT NULL AND share_2020 IS NOT NULL
  ),

  -- Step 4: rank products by total sales (top 20%)
  ranked_products AS (
    SELECT
      prod_id,
      total_sales_both,
      abs_ppt_change,
      NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY total_sales_both DESC) AS sales_quintile
    FROM product_share_change
  ),
  top_20_products AS (
    SELECT
      prod_id,
      abs_ppt_change
    FROM ranked_products
    WHERE sales_quintile = 1
  )

  -- Step 5: get the product with smallest absolute percentage-point change
  SELECT
    pr.prod_id,
    pr.prod_name
  FROM top_20_products t
  JOIN products pr ON t.prod_id = pr.prod_id
  ORDER BY t.abs_ppt_change ASC
  LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Define a CTE to filter sales by required promotions, channels, and France country
WITH filtered_sales AS (
    SELECT
        s."prod_id",
        s."amount_sold",
        s."time_id"
    FROM "sales" s
    INNER JOIN "promotions" p ON s."promo_id" = p."promo_id"
        AND p."promo_total_id" = 1
    INNER JOIN "channels" ch ON s."channel_id" = ch."channel_id"
        AND ch."channel_total_id" = 1
    INNER JOIN "customers" c ON s."cust_id" = c."cust_id"
    INNER JOIN "countries" co ON c."country_id" = co."country_id"
        AND co."country_name" = 'France'
),

-- Step 2: Aggregate sales by product, year, and calendar month for 2019 and 2020
sales_2019_2020 AS (
    SELECT
        "prod_id",
        CAST(strftime('%Y', "time_id") AS INTEGER) AS "year",
        CAST(strftime('%m', "time_id") AS INTEGER) AS "month",
        SUM("amount_sold") AS "total_sales"
    FROM "filtered_sales"
    WHERE "time_id" >= '2019-01-01' AND "time_id" < '2021-01-01'
    GROUP BY "prod_id", "year", "month"
),

-- Step 3: Pivot to get sales for 2019 and 2020 in separate columns per product-month
historical_pivot AS (
    SELECT
        a."prod_id",
        a."month",
        a."total_sales" AS "sales_2019",
        b."total_sales" AS "sales_2020"
    FROM sales_2019_2020 a
    INNER JOIN sales_2019_2020 b
        ON a."prod_id" = b."prod_id"
        AND a."month" = b."month"
        AND a."year" = 2019
        AND b."year" = 2020
),

-- Step 4: Calculate projected 2021 sales using growth formula
projected_2021 AS (
    SELECT
        "prod_id",
        "month",
        "sales_2019",
        "sales_2020",
        -- Projected 2021 = sales_2020 + ((sales_2020 - sales_2019) / sales_2019) * sales_2020
        -- Equivalent to: sales_2020 * (1 + (sales_2020 - sales_2019) / sales_2019)
        CASE
            WHEN "sales_2019" > 0 THEN
                "sales_2020" + ((("sales_2020" - "sales_2019") / "sales_2019") * "sales_2020")
            ELSE
                NULL  -- Cannot calculate growth if 2019 sales are zero; skip such products
        END AS "projected_local"
    FROM "historical_pivot"
),

-- Step 5: Convert projected local currency to USD using 2021 exchange rates
projected_usd AS (
    SELECT
        p."prod_id",
        p."month",
        p."projected_local",
        cur."to_us",
        ROUND(p."projected_local" * cur."to_us", 2) AS "projected_usd"
    FROM "projected_2021" p
    INNER JOIN "currency" cur
        ON cur."country" = 'France'
        AND cur."year" = 2021
        AND cur."month" = p."month"
),

-- Step 6: Average projected USD sales by month across all products
final_averages AS (
    SELECT
        "month",
        ROUND(AVG("projected_usd"), 2) AS "avg_projected_monthly_sales_usd"
    FROM "projected_usd"
    GROUP BY "month"
)

-- Final result: list months 1 to 12 with averages (months with no data will not appear)
SELECT
    "month",
    "avg_projected_monthly_sales_usd"
FROM "final_averages"
ORDER BY "month";
```
</details>

```sql
WITH sales_base AS (
    SELECT
        s."prod_id",
        t."calendar_year",
        t."calendar_month_number",
        SUM(s."amount_sold") AS "monthly_sales"
    FROM "sales" s
    JOIN "times" t ON s."time_id" = t."time_id"
    JOIN "customers" c ON s."cust_id" = c."cust_id"
    JOIN "countries" co ON c."country_id" = co."country_id"
    JOIN "promotions" p ON s."promo_id" = p."promo_id"
    JOIN "channels" ch ON s."channel_id" = ch."channel_id"
    WHERE
        co."country_name" = 'France'
        AND p."promo_total_id" = 1
        AND ch."channel_total_id" = 1
        AND t."calendar_year" IN (2019, 2020)
    GROUP BY
        s."prod_id",
        t."calendar_year",
        t."calendar_month_number"
),

-- Step 2: Separate 2019 and 2020 monthly sales per product
sales_2019 AS (
    SELECT
        "prod_id",
        "calendar_month_number",
        "monthly_sales" AS "sales_2019"
    FROM sales_base
    WHERE "calendar_year" = 2019
),

sales_2020 AS (
    SELECT
        "prod_id",
        "calendar_month_number",
        "monthly_sales" AS "sales_2020"
    FROM sales_base
    WHERE "calendar_year" = 2020
),

-- Step 3: Compute projected 2021 sales (local currency) using growth rate formula
projected AS (
    SELECT
        a."prod_id",
        a."calendar_month_number",
        ((b."sales_2020" - a."sales_2019") / a."sales_2019") * b."sales_2020" + b."sales_2020" AS "projected_sales_local"
    FROM sales_2019 a
    INNER JOIN sales_2020 b
        ON a."prod_id" = b."prod_id" AND a."calendar_month_number" = b."calendar_month_number"
    WHERE a."sales_2019" != 0  -- avoid division by zero
),

-- Step 4: Convert projected sales to USD using currency table for France, 2021
projected_usd AS (
    SELECT
        p."prod_id",
        p."calendar_month_number",
        p."projected_sales_local",
        COALESCE(c."to_us", 1) AS "rate",
        p."projected_sales_local" * COALESCE(c."to_us", 1) AS "projected_sales_usd"
    FROM projected p
    LEFT JOIN "currency" c
        ON c."country" = 'France'
        AND c."year" = 2021
        AND c."month" = p."calendar_month_number"
),

-- Step 5: Average projected sales (USD) per calendar month
monthly_avg AS (
    SELECT
        "calendar_month_number",
        AVG("projected_sales_usd") AS "avg_projected_usd"
    FROM projected_usd
    GROUP BY "calendar_month_number"
),

-- Step 6: Rank monthly averages to compute median (12 months → average of 6th and 7th)
ordered_avgs AS (
    SELECT
        "avg_projected_usd",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "avg_projected_usd") AS "rn",
        COUNT(*) OVER () AS "cnt"
    FROM monthly_avg
    WHERE "avg_projected_usd" IS NOT NULL
)

-- Step 7: Final median
SELECT ROUND(AVG("avg_projected_usd"), 4) AS "median_avg_monthly_projected_sales_usd"
FROM ordered_avgs
WHERE "rn" IN (("cnt" + 1) / 2, ("cnt" + 2) / 2);
```
</details>

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify Italian customers using countries table
WITH italian_customers AS (
    SELECT 
        c.cust_id
    FROM customers c
    INNER JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
    WHERE LOWER(co.country_name) = 'italy'
),

-- Step 2: Calculate profit per sale in December 2021
-- Profit = amount_sold - unit_cost (from costs table linked via promo_id, prod_id, time_id)
december_2021_sales AS (
    SELECT 
        s.cust_id,
        s.time_id,
        s.amount_sold,
        (s.amount_sold - COALESCE(cst.unit_cost, 0)) AS profit
    FROM sales s
    INNER JOIN italian_customers ic ON s.cust_id = ic.cust_id
    LEFT JOIN costs cst ON s.prod_id = cst.prod_id 
        AND s.promo_id = cst.promo_id 
        AND s.channel_id = cst.channel_id 
        AND s.time_id = cst.time_id
    INNER JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
    WHERE t.calendar_month_name = 'December' 
        AND t.calendar_year = 2021
),

-- Step 3: Aggregate total profit per customer for December 2021
customer_profits AS (
    SELECT 
        cust_id,
        SUM(profit) AS total_profit
    FROM december_2021_sales
    GROUP BY cust_id
),

-- Step 4: Segment customers into 10 evenly divided tiers based on total profit
-- NTILE(10) divides rows into 10 equal groups ordered by profit
tiered_customers AS (
    SELECT 
        cust_id,
        total_profit,
        NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY total_profit) AS profit_tier
    FROM customer_profits
    WHERE total_profit IS NOT NULL
)

-- Step 5: Get highest and lowest profit for each tier
SELECT 
    profit_tier,
    ROUND(MAX(total_profit), 4) AS highest_profit,
    ROUND(MIN(total_profit), 4) AS lowest_profit
FROM tiered_customers
GROUP BY profit_tier
ORDER BY profit_tier;
```
</details>

### 207. local071 (DB: `city_legislation`)
**Question**: Could you review our records in June 2022 and identify which countries have the longest streak of consecutive inserted city dates? Please list the 2-letter length country codes of these countries.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| country_code_2   |
|:-----------------|
| br               |
| in               |
| us               |

| US               |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

| country_code_2   |
|:-----------------|
| br               |
| in               |
| us               |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
N/A
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Get distinct inserted dates per country in June 2022
WITH cities_june AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "country_code_2", "insert_date"
    FROM "cities"
    WHERE "insert_date" >= '2022-06-01' AND "insert_date" <= '2022-06-30'
),

-- Step 2: For each country, order dates and compute previous date
dates_ordered AS (
    SELECT 
        "country_code_2",
        "insert_date",
        LAG("insert_date") OVER (
            PARTITION BY "country_code_2" 
            ORDER BY "insert_date"
        ) AS prev_date
    FROM cities_june
),

-- Step 3: Detect gaps (difference > 1 day) to assign group IDs
streak_groups AS (
    SELECT 
        "country_code_2",
        "insert_date",
        SUM(
            CASE 
                WHEN "prev_date" IS NULL 
                     OR julianday("insert_date") - julianday("prev_date") > 1 
                THEN 1 
                ELSE 0 
            END
        ) OVER (
            PARTITION BY "country_code_2" 
            ORDER BY "insert_date"
        ) AS group_id
    FROM dates_ordered
),

-- Step 4: Count consecutive dates in each group (streak length)
streak_lengths AS (
    SELECT 
        "country_code_2",
        "group_id",
        COUNT(*) AS streak_length
    FROM streak_groups
    GROUP BY "country_code_2", "group_id"
),

-- Step 5: Get the maximum streak length per country
max_streak_per_country AS (
    SELECT 
        "country_code_2",
        MAX("streak_length") AS max_streak
    FROM streak_lengths
    GROUP BY "country_code_2"
),

-- Step 6: Find the global maximum streak length across all countries
global_max AS (
    SELECT MAX("max_streak") AS global_max_streak
    FROM max_streak_per_country
)

-- Step 7: Return the 2-letter country codes of countries that achieve the global maximum
SELECT "country_code_2"
FROM max_streak_per_country
WHERE "max_streak" = (SELECT "global_max_streak" FROM global_max)
ORDER BY "country_code_2";
```
</details>

<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|:---------------|-----------------------------:|
| iran           |                          0.2 |

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
N/A
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Find the country (country_code_2) that has exactly 9 distinct insert_dates in Jan 2022
WITH country_9 AS (
    SELECT c2.country_code_2, cc.country_name
    FROM cities c2
    JOIN cities_countries cc ON c2.country_code_2 = cc."country_code_2"
    WHERE c2.insert_date BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2022-01-31'
    GROUP BY c2.country_code_2
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c2.insert_date) = 9
    LIMIT 1
),

-- Step 2: All distinct insert dates for that country in Jan 2022
distinct_dates AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT insert_date
    FROM cities
    WHERE country_code_2 = (SELECT country_code_2 FROM country_9)
      AND insert_date BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2022-01-31'
),

-- Step 3: Group consecutive dates by using island detection
--   julianday(insert_date) - ROW_NUMBER() gives a constant for each group of consecutive days
date_groups AS (
    SELECT insert_date,
           julianday(insert_date) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY insert_date) AS grp
    FROM distinct_dates
),

-- Step 4: Compute start, end, and length of each consecutive block
consecutive_ranges AS (
    SELECT grp,
           MIN(insert_date) AS start_date,
           MAX(insert_date) AS end_date,
           COUNT(*) AS day_count
    FROM date_groups
    GROUP BY grp
),

-- Step 5: Pick the longest consecutive block (ties broken by earliest start)
longest_range AS (
    SELECT start_date, end_date
    FROM consecutive_ranges
    ORDER BY day_count DESC, start_date ASC
    LIMIT 1
)

-- Step 6: Compute the proportion of capital entries within that longest block
SELECT
    (SELECT country_name FROM country_9) AS country_name,
    ROUND(
        (
            SELECT COUNT(*)
            FROM cities
            WHERE country_code_2 = (SELECT country_code_2 FROM country_9)
              AND insert_date BETWEEN (SELECT start_date FROM longest_range) AND (SELECT end_date FROM longest_range)
              AND capital = 1
        ) * 1.0 /
        (
            SELECT COUNT(*)
            FROM cities
            WHERE country_code_2 = (SELECT country_code_2 FROM country_9)
              AND insert_date BETWEEN (SELECT start_date FROM longest_range) AND (SELECT end_date FROM longest_range)
        ), 4
    ) AS proportion_capital_entries;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Generate all combinations of years (2021-2023) and months (April, May, June)
years AS (
    SELECT 2021 AS year
    UNION ALL SELECT 2022
    UNION ALL SELECT 2023
),
months AS (
    SELECT '04' AS month_num, 'April' AS month_name
    UNION ALL SELECT '05', 'May'
    UNION ALL SELECT '06', 'June'
),
all_combos AS (
    SELECT y.year, m.month_num, m.month_name
    FROM years y
    CROSS JOIN months m
),

-- Count new cities per year and month (only April, May, June)
actual_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        CAST(strftime('%Y', "insert_date") AS INTEGER) AS year,
        strftime('%m', "insert_date") AS month_num,
        COUNT(*) AS city_count
    FROM "cities"
    WHERE strftime('%m', "insert_date") IN ('04','05','06')
      AND strftime('%Y', "insert_date") BETWEEN '2021' AND '2023'
    GROUP BY year, month_num
),

-- Combine to ensure every month-year has a count (0 if missing)
monthly_data AS (
    SELECT 
        a.year,
        a.month_name,
        COALESCE(c.city_count, 0) AS city_count
    FROM all_combos a
    LEFT JOIN actual_counts c 
        ON a.year = c.year AND a.month_num = c.month_num
),

-- Compute cumulative running total per month across years
cumulative AS (
    SELECT 
        year,
        month_name,
        city_count,
        SUM(city_count) OVER (
            PARTITION BY month_name 
            ORDER BY year 
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) AS running_total
    FROM monthly_data
),

-- Get previous year's values for YoY calculation
growth_prep AS (
    SELECT 
        year,
        month_name,
        city_count,
        running_total,
        LAG(city_count) OVER (PARTITION BY month_name ORDER BY year) AS prev_city_count,
        LAG(running_total) OVER (PARTITION BY month_name ORDER BY year) AS prev_running_total
    FROM cumulative
)

-- Final output: only 2022 and 2023
SELECT 
    year,
    month_name,
    city_count AS monthly_total,
    running_total,
    ROUND(
        (city_count - prev_city_count) * 100.0 / NULLIF(prev_city_count, 0), 
        4
    ) AS monthly_yoy_growth_percent,
    ROUND(
        (running_total - prev_running_total) * 100.0 / NULLIF(prev_running_total, 0), 
        4
    ) AS running_total_yoy_growth_percent
FROM growth_prep
WHERE year IN (2022, 2023)
ORDER BY year, month_name;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH delivered AS (
    SELECT o.order_id, o.pizza_id, o.exclusions, o.extras
    FROM pizza_clean_customer_orders o
    JOIN pizza_clean_runner_orders r ON o.order_id = r.order_id
    WHERE r.cancellation IS NULL 
       OR r.cancellation = '' 
       OR LOWER(TRIM(r.cancellation)) = 'none'
),
std_toppings AS (
    SELECT d.order_id, d.pizza_id,
           r.toppings AS remaining,
           NULL AS topping_id,
           0 AS lev
    FROM delivered d
    JOIN pizza_recipes r ON d.pizza_id = r.pizza_id
    UNION ALL
    SELECT order_id, pizza_id,
           CASE WHEN instr(remaining, ',') > 0 THEN substr(remaining, instr(remaining, ',')+1) ELSE '' END,
           CASE WHEN instr(remaining, ',') > 0 THEN TRIM(substr(remaining, 1, instr(remaining, ',')-1)) ELSE TRIM(remaining) END,
           lev+1
    FROM std_toppings
    WHERE TRIM(remaining) != ''
),
std_toppings_final AS (
    SELECT order_id, pizza_id, CAST(topping_id AS INTEGER) AS topping_id
    FROM std_toppings
    WHERE topping_id IS NOT NULL AND topping_id != ''
),
exc_toppings AS (
    SELECT d.order_id, d.pizza_id,
           CASE WHEN d.exclusions IS NULL OR TRIM(d.exclusions) = '' OR LOWER(TRIM(d.exclusions)) = 'none' THEN '' ELSE d.exclusions END AS remaining,
           NULL AS topping_id,
           0 AS lev
    FROM delivered d
    UNION ALL
    SELECT order_id, pizza_id,
           CASE WHEN instr(remaining, ',') > 0 THEN substr(remaining, instr(remaining, ',')+1) ELSE '' END,
           CASE WHEN instr(remaining, ',') > 0 THEN TRIM(substr(remaining, 1, instr(remaining, ',')-1)) ELSE TRIM(remaining) END,
           lev+1
    FROM exc_toppings
    WHERE TRIM(remaining) != ''
),
exc_toppings_final AS (
    SELECT order_id, pizza_id, CAST(topping_id AS INTEGER) AS topping_id
    FROM exc_toppings
    WHERE topping_id IS NOT NULL AND topping_id != ''
),
ext_toppings AS (
    SELECT d.order_id, d.pizza_id,
           CASE WHEN d.extras IS NULL OR TRIM(d.extras) = '' OR LOWER(TRIM(d.extras)) = 'none' THEN '' ELSE d.extras END AS remaining,
           NULL AS topping_id,
           0 AS lev
    FROM delivered d
    UNION ALL
    SELECT order_id, pizza_id,
           CASE WHEN instr(remaining, ',') > 0 THEN substr(remaining, instr(remaining, ',')+1) ELSE '' END,
           CASE WHEN instr(remaining, ',') > 0 THEN TRIM(substr(remaining, 1, instr(remaining, ',')-1)) ELSE TRIM(remaining) END,
           lev+1
    FROM ext_toppings
    WHERE TRIM(remaining) != ''
),
ext_toppings_final AS (
    SELECT order_id, pizza_id, CAST(topping_id AS INTEGER) AS topping_id
    FROM ext_toppings
    WHERE topping_id IS NOT NULL AND topping_id != ''
),
toppings_union AS (
    SELECT topping_id, 1 AS sign FROM std_toppings_final
    UNION ALL
    SELECT topping_id, -1 AS sign FROM exc_toppings_final
    UNION ALL
    SELECT topping_id, 1 AS sign FROM ext_toppings_final
),
ingredient_usage AS (
    SELECT topping_id, SUM(sign) AS total_quantity
    FROM toppings_union
    GROUP BY topping_id
    HAVING total_quantity > 0
)
SELECT t.topping_name, i.total_quantity
FROM ingredient_usage i
JOIN pizza_toppings t ON i.topping_id = t.topping_id
```

```sql
WITH 
-- Join customer orders with pizza names to get base price per pizza
base_pizzas AS (
    SELECT
        c.order_id,
        c.pizza_id,
        n.pizza_name,
        CASE
            WHEN LOWER(n.pizza_name) = 'meatlovers' THEN 12
            WHEN LOWER(n.pizza_name) = 'vegetarian' THEN 10
        END AS base_price,
        -- Count extra toppings: number of comma-separated values in extras column
        CASE
            WHEN c.extras IS NULL OR LOWER(c.extras) = 'none' THEN 0
            ELSE LENGTH(c.extras) - LENGTH(REPLACE(c.extras, ',', '')) + 1
        END AS extra_count
    FROM pizza_clean_customer_orders c
    INNER JOIN pizza_names n
        ON c.pizza_id = n.pizza_id
)
-- Filter out canceled orders using the cleaned runner orders table
SELECT
    SUM(base_price + extra_count) AS total_income
FROM base_pizzas bp
INNER JOIN pizza_clean_runner_orders r
    ON bp.order_id = r.order_id
WHERE 
    -- Only include orders that are not canceled
    (r.cancellation IS NULL OR LOWER(r.cancellation) = 'none')
    -- Only consider the two pizza types with defined prices
    AND bp.pizza_name IN ('Meatlovers', 'Vegetarian');
```
